User ran the live-booking-availability test suggested in the prior entry. Checked recreation.gov's per-day availability table directly (not just the summary calendar text) for two dates: (1) 4/21/2027 -- before both proposed seasons, so non-discriminating as expected -- Cottonwood Lakes and Cottonwood Pass both show a released value of 0 (confirmed no quota, not 'NR'). (2) 9/21-24/2026 -- inside the discriminating window (after Sep15, before Nov1) -- Cottonwood Lakes and Cottonwood Pass show 'NR' on all 4 days. Per the page's own legend, NR = 'Not Yet Released', a distinct status from 'Unavailable' -- it means the system hasn't opened booking for that date, not that the date is confirmed out of season. Critically, the SAME 4 dates for Deer Lakes (a plain John Muir Wilderness trail, general Inyo system) already show real released numbers (6, 6, NR, 6) one row below -- meaning the 6-month advance window is clearly already open system-wide for that date range, yet Cottonwood specifically has not released for it. This is strong (not fully conclusive, since NR could in principle still resolve to a nonzero number later) structural evidence that Cottonwood Lakes/Cottonwood Pass run on a DIFFERENT release/quota mechanism than standard JM-coded trails, consistent with -- and further supporting -- the shorter GT-specific season already adopted in permits.csv. Does not upgrade the resolution to full certainty, but adds a third independent data point (live booking system behavior, not just static documents) pointing the same direction as the two PDF sources.

First independent verification of this permit_group (previously web-search synthesis only). CORRECTS the reservation mechanism: the 60% portion was modeled as a simple rolling reservation window (like Inyo/SEKI); it's actually a WEEKLY LOTTERY -- each week-long hiking-start window gets its own application period (opens Sunday 12:01am, closes the following Saturday 11:59pm, ~24 weeks/168 days ahead, results by Monday 5pm), with lottery-unclaimed spots opening first-come the following Friday up to 3 days out, and the remaining 40% released 7 days out (up to 3 days before entry). Structurally closer to the Whitney Zone lottery than to Inyo's system, just weekly instead of annual. ALSO CORRECTS an implicit assumption: season start is NOT a fixed May 1 park-wide -- source states late-April starts are available 'in some -- but not all -- areas of the park', with exact per-area dates in a downloadable dataset (linked from the source page, not retrieved). 05-01 in this row is now flagged as an approximation, not confirmed. permits.py gained a Yosemite-specific status branch so the report says 'apply to the weekly lottery' instead of the generic 'book now', matching the Whitney/CPMA precedent for permits whose mechanism doesn't fit the generic rolling-reservation model.

This project currently asserts year-round, siding with two sources against the land manager's own page -- normally the land manager would win on a regulatory question, which is why this is logged rather than resolved. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE CAVEAT: the Eldorado NF text was read via a web-search snippet, not a direct page fetch (blocked from this environment), so it needs a first-hand read before being acted on. Eldorado NF's camping page states the California Campfire Permit requirement in full, and reading it exposed that this project had the rule WRONG in five places and inconsistent across seven. CORRECTS THE SCOPE: the permit covers campfires, stoves, LANTERNS and BARBEQUES -- five permit_groups described it as applying to a 'stove' alone. CORRECTS THE EXEMPTION: it is required outside a campground or RV *and in some developed campgrounds*, so 'outside a developed campground' was not a safe exemption as previously written. ADDS two facts held nowhere: the signer must be 18 or older (a group of minors cannot self-issue), and the legal basis is 36 CFR 261.52(k) / PRC 4433. URL CORRECTION: this project carried three different links for one permit (fs.usda.gov/main/r5/passes-permits on the 'none' group, readyforwildfire.org on gtw_free, nothing on the rest), and the Eldorado NF page itself cites 'www.preventwildfiresca.org', which does not resolve. The working path is readyforwildfire.org/prevent-wildfire/campfire-safety, which links through to the permit portal at permit.preventwildfiresca.org -- so gtw_free's link was the closest to right all along. STRUCTURAL FIX: because this is California state law rather than a per-wilderness rule, it is now stored once in data/regulations.csv scoped to the CA jurisdiction and inherited by every group, and the seven duplicated copies have been removed. ALSO ADDS an Eldorado NF-wide rule: dispersed camping outside a developed campground is capped at 10 days per ranger district per calendar year.

Ordinance 38 (Rules and Regulations, revised September 2023), Sections 801-803, read in full from a PDF supplied by the user. THE FIRST REGULATION SOURCE THIS PROJECT HAS FOR EBRPD AT ALL: its two trailheads previously resolved exactly one rule, the statewide California Campfire Permit, because nothing else had ever been scoped to them. CORRECTS THIS PROJECT'S OWN FRAMING OF THE PETS CATEGORY, which was built entirely from Forest Service dog rules and assumed agencies legislate about dogs. Ordinance 38 does not: it writes 'no dog, cat, or other animal' in 801.1 and 801.2(h)-(i), so a cat is a named subject of the rule rather than an animal the reader has to reason across from a dog leash law. THE RULE THAT ACTUALLY ANSWERS THE CAMPGROUND QUESTION is 801.2(i): at campgrounds, dogs, cats or other animals must be attended and either leashed OR contained within a vehicle, tent or other physical confinement -- confinement is an accepted alternative to a leash, which a leash-only reading would have got wrong. TWO ASYMMETRIES FOUND, both of which cut against reading the ordinance as species-neutral throughout, and both recorded rather than smoothed over: the three-per-person cap in 801.2(d) is written for DOGS, and the leash-optional allowance for undeveloped areas in 801.3 opens 'A dog may run at large', so a cat has no off-leash provision anywhere in the District. ADDS the prohibited-area list (801.1 plus Attachment B), which bars every animal, leashed or not, from swim areas, bathing beaches, designated nature study areas, wetlands and marshes, and golf courses; Del Valle Beaches/Swim Area is named explicitly, which matters because Del Valle is this project's own East Bay trailhead. Service animals assisting disabled persons are exempt. ADDS the six-foot leash maximum (801.2(f)), electronic collars explicitly excluded from counting as a restraint (801.2(e)), extendable leashes permitted only if not extended past six feet (801.2(g)), the ~200 ft leash radius around any parking lot, trail head or staging area (801.2), the bar on leaving any animal unattended and uncontained (801.2(h)), and immediate removal of dog excrement (801.10). EIGHTEEN PARKS OFFER CAMPING; this project holds campgrounds for four of them (Del Valle, Sunol, Mission Peak, Ohlone). The twelve with no campground row here are Black Diamond Mines, Briones, Charles Lee Tilden, Coyote Hills, Dr. Aurelia Reinhardt Redwood, Dry Creek Pioneer, Garin, Las Trampas, Morgan Territory, Point Pinole, Round Valley and Tilden Nature Area. NOT ADDED, deliberately: the listing names parks, not campgrounds, and gives no campground name, site count, fee, reservation channel or coordinates for any of them. A campground row invented from a park name would assert a facility this project cannot name. They need each park's own camping page. A SECOND SIGNAL WORTH CHECKING BUT NOT ENCODED: the listing carries a per-park 'Dogs Allowed' attribute, and four camping parks lack it -- Las Trampas, Round Valley, Sunol and Tilden Nature Area. Ordinance 38's Attachment B independently corroborates two of those (Round Valley outright as a wildlife protection area for listed species at risk, and the Tilden Botanical Garden and Nature Area), partially corroborates Las Trampas (Attachment B lists only Las Trampas Stables, not the preserve, so the icon is stricter than the ordinance), and does not mention Sunol at all. A missing amenity icon is not a stated rule, and the gap between the icon and the ordinance is itself the reason not to encode it as one.

ADDS TWO DRIVE-IN CAMPGROUNDS, the first in this dataset outside the Ohlone corridor: Anthony Chabot Campground and Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay. Anthony Chabot matters to the question this project was pointed at -- it is the nearest drive-in camping to Oakland in the dataset, where Del Valle is roughly twice as far. WEAK PROVENANCE, STATED AS SUCH: every fact in both rows comes from web-search summaries of EBRPD pages, not from the pages themselves, which this environment cannot reach. Both rows carry a source_url to check against and a BLANK verified_date, and campgrounds.csv gained those two columns in this change -- it previously had no provenance columns at all, so its seven existing rows cited nothing. Those stay blank rather than being given an invented citation. FIELDS LEFT EMPTY RATHER THAN GUESSED: fee_notes, check-in and check-out times, and the nightly entry cutoff. A blank fee already renders as 'NO FEE ON FILE -- absent is not free'. TWO CAVEATS CARRIED IN THE ROWS THEMSELVES. Anthony Chabot's reported 75 sites include 10 hike-in ones, so access_mode is not uniform within the campground; the row is tagged drive_in for the other 65 and says so. Dumbarton Quarry's park field is genuinely ambiguous: EBRPD lists it as a park in its own right while describing it as located within Coyote Hills Regional Park, which appears separately in the same listing with its own camping. Since the park field is what campgrounds join to park_access and trailheads on, the ambiguity is flagged in the row rather than resolved by picking one. Both parks were added to the referential-integrity allowlist for parks that have a campground but no trailhead, the same shape Sunol already had, rather than inventing park_access rows whose fees nobody knows.

EBRPD's Reservations page, pasted in full. THE CHANNEL FACTS ARE NOW FIRST-HAND rather than inherited from trip notes, and they split by campsite type, which this project had recorded only implicitly. Family campsites are booked at reserveamerica.com or by phone; GROUP AND BACKPACK CAMPSITES ARE PHONE ONLY and are not bookable online at all, which confirms what the six Ohlone corridor rows already said ('phone, confirmed via ReserveAmerica') and now states it on the District's own authority. ADDS A TRAP THE README'S OWN FALSIFICATION LIST NAMES: there is a published reservations email address, reservations@ebparks.org, and it accepts NO reservations -- general inquiries only. Someone who emails it and waits has not booked anything. ADDS a third channel nobody here had: in-person walk-in service at District HQ, 2950 Peralta Oaks Ct., Oakland. ADDS the current booking horizon: group and backpack campsites are taking arrival dates through December 2026, and event venues through December 2027. Recorded with its as-of date because a rolling horizon is a fact that expires. ADDS a dated closure of the reservations phone line, Wednesday 14 October 2026 9am-12pm, which matters only because that line is the sole channel for backpack sites. NOT CAPTURED, as it does not change a trip plan for this project's objectives: picnic-site and event-venue booking, activity registration, and the in-District fee waiver for organizations hosting events for people with disabilities, seniors or low-income groups -- a real exemption, but on reservation fees for group events rather than on anything a camping party pays. STRUCTURAL NOTE, NOT A FACT ABOUT EBRPD: the contact string this entry sharpens is District-wide and is now stored in nine campground rows, and will be in twenty-one once the remaining parks land. That is the same shape as the California Campfire Permit copied into seven permits.csv rows, which is what regulations.csv was built to stop. Booking mechanics have no agency-scoped home in this schema; they need one.

TWO EBRPD PAGES DISAGREE ON HOW MANY PARKS OFFER CAMPING. The Reservations page states the department oversees 'a range of camping opportunities including backpacking, family, group, and equestrian camping at 15 parks'. The park finder filtered by the camping activity returns 18 parks: Anthony Chabot, Black Diamond Mines, Briones, Charles Lee Tilden, Coyote Hills, Del Valle, Dr. Aurelia Reinhardt Redwood, Dry Creek Pioneer, Dumbarton Quarry, Garin, Las Trampas, Mission Peak, Morgan Territory, Ohlone, Point Pinole, Round Valley, Sunol and Tilden Nature Area. Both were read on 2026-09-15. NEITHER FIGURE IS TAKEN AS CORRECT HERE. The gap is three, and the reconciliation is not obvious: the finder may tag a park whose camping the Reservations department does not handle, Dumbarton Quarry is listed as a park in its own right while sitting inside Coyote Hills so one arrangement could be double-counted, or Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer are described by the District as a single paired parkland yet appear as two entries. WHY IT MATTERS rather than being trivia: the difference decides whether a park showing a camping icon can actually be booked, which is the question someone acts on. RESOLVED BY going park by park through each camping page and counting what is bookable -- in progress at the time of writing.

Anthony Chabot's park page, pasted in full, plus its map brochure PDF reached from that page (AnthonyChabot-LakeChabot-LeonaCanyon-map-brochure.pdf). PROMOTES THE ANTHONY CHABOT CAMPGROUND ROW FROM WEB-SEARCH GUESSWORK TO A FIRST-HAND READ: it was added earlier today with a blank verified_date and every field caveated, and now carries fees, gate hours and facilities from EBRPD's own text. ADDS THE FEE SCHEDULE, which had been blank rather than guessed: drive-in camping $35/night, hike-in $25/night, RV hook-up $45/night, limited overflow parking $8/night/vehicle, RV sewage disposal $20/use, firewood $10/bundle and charcoal $15/bag at the campground kiosk. The three camping rates confirm that access_mode is genuinely mixed inside this one campground -- EBRPD prices hike-in sites separately -- which the row already said on weaker evidence. ADDS A GATE CUTOFF STATED BY THE AGENCY, unlike Del Valle's, which this project holds only as a visitor's near-miss report: campground gates close at 10:00pm, and campground and group camp gate hours run 8am-10pm, so there is no arrival before 8am either, while the park itself is open 5am-10pm. ADDS AN RV CONSTRAINT held nowhere in this project: maximum vehicle length 35 feet on hookup sites, with sewage, water and 30-amp electric. ADDS a park_access row, which removes Anthony Chabot from the referential-integrity allowlist for parks with a campground and no trailhead. PARKING IS FREE HERE, and that is a fact about this park rather than about the District: Del Valle charges $10 on weekends and holidays, and Lake Chabot -- connected by trail and covered by the same brochure -- charges $5/vehicle. A reader generalising either way is wrong. CONFIRMS Ordinance 38 s.400.3(b) from a second, independent document: the brochure states the same 15 consecutive days / 30 days per year / 2-day break stay limit, so it is left as the single agency-scoped rule rather than copied into the campground row. CORRECTS THE GROUP BOOKING LEAD TIME: the reservations page gives 2 business days for campsites generally, while this brochure requires group camping reservations at least 3 business days in advance. Recorded as a difference between site classes rather than a conflict, since booking_channels.csv now holds lead time per class. The brochure's rules panel restates Ordinance 38's dog leash rules (200 ft, developed areas, grazing areas, clean up after your pet) with no drift, so no regulation row changed. NOT CAPTURED: Lake Chabot's own fees, boat rental, fishing and tour-boat operations, and the equestrian centres -- none of them change a camping plan. ALSO NOT CAPTURED, AND THIS ONE IS A SCHEMA GAP RATHER THAN A CHOICE: the page's top carries live trail-closure notices, updated 2026-09-15 -- Willowview Trail closed, Redtail Trail closed between Brandon and Grass Valley, 300 ft of Brandon Trail inaccessible to equestrians, and a permanently closed section of Bird Trail since 2025-08-04. The scorecard already reports 'What is closed?' as no-model for every objective in the dataset, and this is that gap in concrete form: there is nowhere to put a dated closure. The notices also sit under no heading on the page, so a future scrape has nothing to anchor on.

EBMUD's trail use permit page, pasted in full. A NEW AGENCY AND A NEW PERMIT, and the first in this project issued by a water utility rather than a park or forest agency. It arrives through Anthony Chabot rather than being sought out: the six-mile Chabot-to-Garin Regional Trail linking Anthony Chabot to Cull Canyon crosses EBMUD watershed land and requires this permit, and EBRPD's own Ordinance 38 Attachment C already named EBMUD first among lands owned by others whose rules apply once crossed. TWO THINGS HERE ARE THE KIND THIS PROJECT EXISTS TO CATCH. First, the fee ladder has a free rung that is NOT SOLD THROUGH THE CHECKOUT that sells every other tier: $3/day, $10/year, $20/3yr and $30/5yr are bought online at trailpermits.ebmud.com, while the income-qualified $0 one-year permit requires downloading a PDF, completing it and MAILING it. Someone entitled to pay nothing cannot obtain it the way everyone else obtains theirs, and has to allow post time -- a channel difference, not just a price. Second, THE PERMIT COVERS ONE NAMED PERSON, who may bring immediate family plus three guests and is responsible for their conduct, and is not transferable; a party of five unrelated people needs more than one. Both facts are stored in the fields built for them rather than in prose. ADDS the income thresholds verbatim ($67,900 for 1-2 people rising to $98,450 for 6, plus $6,800 per additional member) because a reader has to check themselves against them. ADDS the exclusion that no permit is required for the Lafayette Reservoir Rim or Lakeside Trail, which is the kind of over-application a permit row invites. NO TRAILHEAD USES THIS GROUP YET: nothing in trailheads.csv sits on EBMUD land, so the row is currently reachable only by reading it. That is deliberate -- the permit is real and sourced, and inventing a trailhead to justify it would be the wrong fix. NOT CAPTURED: Mokelumne-area trail permits beyond the contact number, and the Trail Leader permit scheme, which is for organised trips rather than a private party.

Anthony Chabot's Attractions section, pasted in full, completing the read of this park page. CONFIRMS THE SITE COMPOSITION THIS PROJECT HAD BEEN CARRYING AS UNCONFIRMED and corrects one figure in it. EBRPD states 53 drive-to tent sites, 10 walk-to tent sites and 12 RV/trailer sites with full hookups -- 75 in total, matching the web-search figure. But that figure also placed 1 developed group site inside the 75, and it is not there: 53+10+12 accounts for all of them, and the park's seven group camps are separate bookings. A small correction, and exactly the kind a search summary introduces. ADDS that every site has a picnic table and a fire ring with grill. SHARPENS THE GATE RULE FROM A CUTOFF INTO A LOCK-OUT, which changes what a late arrival means: gates are locked at 10pm and NO entry is possible until 8am, but campers may EXIT at any time. A late departure is fine; a late arrival is a night in the car outside the gate. The row previously said only that gates close at 10pm. ADDS GROUP CAMPING as a class this project could not previously describe: seven group camps at 35 to 300 campers, all with picnic tables, BBQ, fire ring, water and chemical or vault toilets, requiring a MINIMUM OF 10 PEOPLE -- so they are not an option for a small party, whatever their capacity suggests. Only one is named, Bort Meadow Group Camp, which is added as a row and is the only EBRPD equestrian camping this project holds outside Del Valle; the other six are unnamed here and no rows were invented for them. CONFIRMS independently that group campsites cannot be reserved online, which booking_channels.csv already stated from the reservations page. AN INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: the same page says the park is 20 minutes from downtown Oakland in its overview and the campground 35 minutes from downtown Oakland and the airport in this section. Both are in the campground's notes. No conflict thread was opened, because drive time gates no decision this project models -- unlike the 25-vs-30 ft setback, where the number is the rule. ADDS the trail context that led to the EBMUD permit logged at ebmud_trail-2026-09-15-01: the East Bay Skyline National Trail runs the length of the park, and the Chabot-to-Garin Regional Trail reaches Cull Canyon over six miles of EBMUD watershed land requiring that permit. NOT CAPTURED: the two equestrian centres, which board horses and give lessons rather than gating any trip.

Anthony Chabot's campground page, pasted in full. REVERSES A CORRECTION THIS PROJECT MADE EARLIER TODAY AND GOT WRONG. Web search had reported the campground's 75 sites as including '1 developed group site'; the park page's Attractions section listed 53 drive-to tent, 10 walk-to tent and 12 RV, which sums to 75 on its own, and that arithmetic was used to strike the group site as a search-summary error. It was not an error -- this page lists it, and it is Puma Point, which sits inside the family campground and now has its own row. The page's own list therefore sums to 76 while calling itself 75. The individual-site figures agree across both pages and are what the row carries; the discrepancy is a counting choice about whether a group site inside the campground is one of its campsites, and it is stated rather than silently resolved. The lesson is the project's own: arithmetic that works is not evidence, and a second source beat a clean sum. NAMES ALL SEVEN GROUP CAMPS WITH THEIR FEES, where only Bort Meadow had been nameable: Puma Point $100 (developed), El Venado $75, Lookout Ridge $75, Two Rocks $75, Lost Ridge $125, Hawk Ridge $175, Bort Meadow $200, each plus an $8 reservation fee. Six rows added, Bort Meadow's fee filled. ADDS A CHARGE THAT DOUBLES THE MONEY NEEDED: every group reservation requires a security/damage deposit equal to one night's fee, so Bort Meadow is $400 to hold rather than $200. ADDS the $8 per-site reservation fee on family bookings, which this row did not carry. ADDS check-in 2pm and check-out 12pm, previously blank. CLARIFIES THE HIKE-IN SITES: #13-22 are explicitly NOT backpack sites -- they are inside the campground without vehicle access or adjacent parking -- which is why access_mode is mixed here. ADDS that generators and smoking are prohibited outright, stricter than Ordinance 38 s.400.2's disturbance test, and that there is NO CAMP STORE beyond the kiosk's firewood and charcoal. ADDS the primitive group camps' character: behind the group camp gate, outside the family campground, no showers or flush toilets, and no RVs, trailers or motorhomes at any group site. ADDS Puma Point's own terms: beer and wine but no hard alcohol, 13 parking passes with the reservation, and no buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks or caterers. NOT READ: the campground map PDF linked from this page (AChabot-Camp-Map.pdf) contains no extractable text -- it is an image -- so nothing was taken from it. NOT CAPTURED: the Lake Chabot blue-green algae caution advisory posted at the time of reading, for the same reason the trail closures were not -- there is nowhere to put a dated advisory, and 'What is closed?' remains no-model on the scorecard. Swimming is never permitted at Lake Chabot regardless of the advisory.

ONE PAGE STATES ANTHONY CHABOT'S QUIET HOURS TWICE AND DIFFERENTLY. The Hours block near the top gives 'Quiet Hours: 10pm - 5am'; the Campground Hours block lower down gives 'Quiet hours: 10pm - 7am'. Same page, same read, two hours apart at the morning end. Internal rather than cross-source, so the document has already discredited its own statement and no ranking of publishers helps. IT MATTERS because it decides when a camper may start packing, run a tap, or drive out: at 5am the early start is legitimate, at 7am it is a violation, and Ordinance 38 s.400.5 allows removal from a campsite for breaking campground rules with no refund and a 15-day ban. Neither figure is stored as the answer. Resolving it needs the posted sign at the campground or a call to the park office on (510) 690-6676.

TWO EBRPD PAGES DISAGREE ON THE MINIMUM PARTY SIZE FOR A GROUP CAMPSITE. Anthony Chabot's park page says 'a minimum of 10 people to use the group campsites'; its campground page says 'A minimum of 17 people are required to reserve a group campsite'. A third statement, on the District's group campsites page, says group sites are for groups of 10 or more while also encouraging groups of 17 or more away from family campgrounds -- which is how 10 and 17 both end up in circulation without either being obviously wrong. IT MATTERS DIRECTLY: a party of twelve either can or cannot book a group site, and the two answers differ on whether they must instead take family sites. Recorded against the campgrounds rather than a permit because EBRPD issues no permit here. Resolving it needs Reservations on (888) 327-2757 option 2, which is the only channel that sells group sites anyway.

HOW LONG AN RV FITS AT ANTHONY CHABOT HAS TWO ANSWERS. The park brochure states a maximum vehicle length of 35 feet on hookup sites. The campground page states that parking pads average 30 feet and the largest is 39. The two are not flatly contradictory -- a pad can be longer than the longest vehicle allowed on it -- but they cannot both be acted on: an owner of a 38-foot rig reads a fit from one and a refusal from the other, and the campground page never says which sites the 39-foot pad belongs to or whether it has hookups. IT MATTERS because the failure is discovered after towing the rig there, which is the class of error this project exists to prevent, and because the 12 hookup sites are the only ones with sewer and electric. Neither figure is stored as the answer; both are in the campground's notes. Resolving it needs the park office on (510) 690-6676 or the per-site dimensions on the ReserveAmerica listing, a1.reserveamerica.com/explore/anthony-chabot/EB/110004/overview.

Anthony Chabot's ReserveAmerica listing, the booking system EBRPD actually sells through, pasted in full. It repeats the campground page's facilities text verbatim, which is itself useful -- the two surfaces agree -- and then adds a page of operational terms that appear nowhere on ebparks.org. ADDS CANCELLATION AND CHANGE MECHANICS, and booking_channels.csv gains a change_cancel column to hold them. The scorecard reports 'Can I change or cancel, and by when?' as NO-MODEL for every objective in this dataset; this is the first data that question has ever had. The answer splits by channel, which is why it belongs here: a family campsite CAN be cancelled online but CANNOT be changed online, and backpacking, equestrian and group reservations can be neither -- all of those need a phone call in office hours. The published email address accepts no cancellations or changes either, matching the fact that it accepts no bookings. ADDS A CLAUSE THAT VOIDS A RESERVATION: bookings are for personal use only, and any resale, transfer, for-profit use or unapproved membership arrangement is cancelled immediately without notice, refund or reimbursement. EBRPD states there are currently NO approved third-party vendors, so any site bought from one is void -- the buyer finds out on arrival. Public advertising of a reservation, social media included, needs a special event permit on file. ADDS the online booking window: 12 weeks ahead to 48 hours before arrival. That 48 hours sits against the reservations page's '2 business days', which differ over a weekend; both are recorded in lead_time with the observation that they may split by channel, flagged as a reading rather than a stated fact. Group lead time has the same shape, '3 days' here against '3 business days' on ebparks.org. ADDS group stay limits of 7 nights per month, distinct from the family campground's 15 consecutive days, and that a group booking's GATE CODE and parking passes are emailed only 5-7 days before arrival. ADDS that group sites need an additional beer and wine permit bought in advance. ADDS site limits that cancel bookings rather than warning: a maximum of two family campsites per household, customer name, primary occupant or registered vehicle on any date, one per date for other site types, and additional sites are cancelled. ADDS 2 vehicles per campsite, hike-in sites #13-22 being 0.2 miles (about 1,000 feet) from parking with a wagon suggested, tents only on dirt or designated pads and never on lawns, fires only from commercially bought wood with WOOD COLLECTION PROHIBITED -- the opposite of the Eldorado NF allowance this project holds -- beer and wine only at 21+, and LIMITED TO NO CELL SERVICE, which matters for a party expecting to look anything up on arrival. ADDS A PET DISTINCTION ORDINANCE 38 DOES NOT DRAW, carried onto ebrpd-pets-prohibited-areas: emotional support animals are NOT service animals for the exemption, and are barred from swim beaches, swim areas, select trails and cabins, while service animals with specialized training are permitted everywhere. ADDS, for dogs specifically, that they must be CONFINED TO VEHICLE OR TENT DURING QUIET HOURS rather than merely leashed -- stricter than Ordinance 38 s.801.2(i)'s leash-or-contain, and stated for dogs only, so whether it reaches a cat is unknown and the campground row says so. NOT CAPTURED: the fire-danger and blue-green-algae advisories, for the same reason as every other dated notice -- there is nowhere to put one.

CLOSES chabot-rv-length. The booking system states 'No rigs over 35 feet in length' twice, in its alert banner and again under Day Passes, agreeing with the park brochure's maximum vehicle length of 35 feet. That is two independent surfaces on the same number against the campground page's 'parking pads average 30 feet; the largest is 39 feet', which on this reading was never a competing limit at all: it describes the length of the pad, not what may be parked on it, and a pad can exceed the longest vehicle allowed on it. 35 FEET IS THE RULE and is stored as such; the 39-foot pad stays in the notes as a dimension, not a permission. The conflict was worth opening -- an owner of a 38-foot rig could have read a fit out of the pad figure -- and it is worth closing on evidence rather than leaving open for tidiness.

CLOSES ebrpd-group-camp-minimum at 17 PEOPLE. The booking system states 'A minimum of 17 people are required to reserve a group campsite' and, separately, that 'Groups larger than 16 should reserve a group campsite' -- two statements on one page agreeing with each other and with Anthony Chabot's campground page. Against that, the park page's 'a minimum of 10 people to use the group campsites' stands alone. Three surfaces to one, and the dissenting one is descriptive prose on a park overview while the agreeing ones are the campground's own terms and the system that enforces them at booking. 17 is stored. The park page's 10 is recorded here rather than erased, because it is still published and a reader may meet it: a party of twelve reading that page would believe it could book a group site, and the booking system is where they would find out otherwise.

IS ANTHONY CHABOT OPEN IN WINTER? The booking system states the campground is CLOSED SEASONALLY FROM 1 NOVEMBER TO 1 APRIL, with select sites closed through May, and describes it as 'a beautiful seasonal public campground'. The park's own map brochure states that 'Year-round camping is available in a eucalyptus grove overlooking Lake Chabot'. Those cannot both be acted on, and this is the most trip-blocking disagreement in this dataset: five months of the year are either bookable or not. THE CLOSURE IS TREATED AS LIVE while the conflict is open, which is the deliberate asymmetry -- believing the brochure and driving to a locked gate costs the trip, while believing the booking system costs an unnecessary look elsewhere. The booking system is also the surface that would refuse the reservation, and it carries the more specific claim, down to which sites reopen when. Neither is dated, so newer-source-wins cannot settle it. Resolving it needs the park office on (510) 690-6676, or an attempt to book a January date, which the system itself would answer.

OVERFLOW PARKING AT ANTHONY CHABOT: PRICED, OR ABSENT? The park brochure lists 'Limited overflow parking: $8/night/vehicle' among its fees and the campground page says reservations are recommended for it, while the booking system states flatly 'No overflow parking available.' A fee schedule does not usually price a facility that does not exist, so the likeliest readings are that overflow parking was withdrawn and the brochure is stale, or that it is seasonal and absent when the campground reopens -- but neither is stated, and the brochure carries no date. IT MATTERS on arrival: two vehicles per campsite is the hard limit, so a party arriving in three cars either pays $8 for the third or has nowhere to put it, and finds out at a gate that locks at 10pm. Both claims are in the campground's notes; neither is stored as the answer.

Anthony Chabot's per-site listing on the booking system, pasted in full with a screenshot of the filter counts. SETTLES THE SITE-COUNT QUESTION THIS PROJECT HAS NOW BEEN WRONG ABOUT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The filters count ALL 76 = 7 group + 11 RV hookup + 10 tent-only + 48 tent/no-hookup, and the listing itself was enumerated site by site to check that: Loop A holds 11 RV sites, Loop B 10 hike-in, and Loops C, D and F 9, 26 and 13 tent sites, which is 48. Every filter total is reproduced by the listing. AGAINST THE PROSE: 12 RV + 53 drive-up tent + 10 hike-in is exactly 75, so the '1 developed group site' the campground page lists inside those 75 does not belong there. Puma Point is real -- this project was right to restore it after striking it this morning -- but it is a separate unit, not one of the 75 individual campsites. The original strike had the arithmetic right and the conclusion wrong; the reversal had the facility right and the arithmetic wrong. Both halves are now in the row. A COINCIDENCE WORTH NAMING SO NOBODY RECONCILES IT FALSELY: the system's 'ALL 76' is not the prose's accidental 76. The system counts 69 listed individual sites plus 7 group camps; the prose's faulty list counts 75 individual sites plus Puma Point. Two different quantities that happen to match. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST IS WHAT IS MISSING: only 69 of the 75 individual sites appear online. Sites 010, 031, 033, 039, 053 and 075 are absent from the booking system's list entirely. Browsing online therefore does not show the full inventory, and a party concluding the campground is full has checked 69 of 75. Why they are absent is NOT STATED by any source: the likeliest reading is that they are the accessible sites, since this same system says ADA campsites must be reserved by phone only and the brochure confirms accessible sites exist here, but that is a hypothesis and the row says so -- they could equally be closed or out of service. ADDS THE LOOP STRUCTURE, which no ebparks.org page carries: Loop A 1-12 (RV, 30-amp full hookup), Loop B 13-22 ('Hike-In Sites (NO driving to site)'), Loop C 23-33, Loop D 34-61, Loop F 62-75, all tent. There is no Loop E. RESOLVES THE GROUP CAMP CAPACITY RANGE into per-site figures, where '35 to 300' was all this project held: El Venado 35, Lookout Ridge 35, Puma Point 50, Two Rocks 50, Lost Ridge 100, Hawk Ridge 100, Bort Meadow 300. CONFIRMS PETS AT EVERY SITE: all 76 listings carry the Pets Allowed marker, group camps and hike-in sites included, with no exception. NOT ADDED AS ROWS: 69 individual campsites. Within a loop the listing differentiates them by nothing at all -- same amenities, same loop, same marker -- and campsites.csv exists for sites that genuinely differ, as Sunol's do by water and restroom proximity. Sixty-nine near-identical rows would be the placeholder pattern this project refuses elsewhere. The loop structure carries the distinction that matters.

EVIDENCE ON THE OPEN SEASON CONFLICT, WHICH IT STRENGTHENS WITHOUT CLOSING. The booking system labels six of Anthony Chabot's seven group camps by season: El Venado, Hawk Ridge, Lookout Ridge, Lost Ridge and Two Rocks are each 'Primitive Group Camp Seasonal A', and Bort Meadow is 'Primitive Group Camp Seasonal B'. Puma Point, the developed one, carries no seasonal label at all. That EBRPD operates named seasons here, and more than one of them, sits badly with the park brochure's flat claim that year-round camping is available, and sits comfortably with the booking system's statement that the campground closes 1 November to 1 April with select sites closed through May -- 'select sites' is what a per-site seasonal designation produces. IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE CONFLICT: what seasons A and B actually run is nowhere stated, no date is attached to either label, and none of this speaks directly to the family campground, which is the part someone car camping would book. The closure stays stored as live. Resolving it still needs the park office on (510) 690-6676, or an attempt to book a January family site.

REVERSES THIS PROJECT'S DECISION NOT TO STORE ANTHONY CHABOT'S SITES INDIVIDUALLY. That call was made on the grounds that sites within a loop differ by nothing, which is true and was the wrong test: the question a reader asks is not 'how does site 45 differ from site 46' but 'what IS site 45', and loop-level prose cannot answer it. Seventy-five rows added to campsites.csv, the first campground here to have them besides Sunol. campsites.csv gains loop, site_type, hookups and online_bookable. THE TYPE VOCABULARY IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE BOOKING SYSTEM'S. ReserveAmerica calls the ten walk-in sites 'Tent Only' and the forty-eight drive-up tent sites 'Tent/No-Hookup', so a reader filtering for a tent site on the more tent-sounding label gets the ten that are a thousand feet from their car. Stored as tent_hike_in and tent_drive_up, with the system's own wording recorded here rather than propagated. THE SIX UNLISTED SITES GET ROWS TOO, which is the point of doing this at all: 010, 031, 033, 039, 053 and 075 exist but never appear online, and a table built only from the listing would rebuild the listing's blind spot inside this project. They carry their loop, which follows from the ranges each loop states, and a BLANK site_type -- not the type of their neighbours. Loop A's other eleven sites are all RV hookup, and that is not evidence about 010. Capacity is 8 on every row, from the stated maximum of 8 people per family campsite, infants and children included. SURFACE CHANGE: plan now summarises a campground of more than twelve sites by type and loop instead of listing them, because 75 site numbers would bury the campground's own facts. Sunol's seven named sites still read one by one. The summary line for the unlisted six says they are absent from the listing with the reason unrecorded, NOT that they are phone-only -- that remains a hypothesis, and the listing shows what is there, never why something is not.

The 'Alerts and Important Information' block at the foot of the filtered campsite listing. IT IS THE SAME TEXT as the ADDITIONAL INFORMATION section already read on the overview page -- ReserveAmerica repeats one boilerplate block on every page of the booking flow. All twenty-one substantive claims in it were checked one by one against this project's data and every one was already stored, and stored somewhere usable -- campground rows and regulation rows -- rather than only in a log summary, which would be provenance without an answer. NOTHING DRIFTED between the two renderings. RE-READING IT DID FIND ONE REAL GAP, which is the reason to check rather than wave a duplicate through. The juveniles rule was being carried only on the seven group camp rows, because it arrived here as part of the group camping text. It is not a group rule: Ordinance 38 s.400.4 makes it agency-wide, and it governs the family campground and the Ohlone backpack camps just as much. It was read first-hand in the ordinance at none-2026-09-15-03 and silently not captured then -- that entry listed what it deliberately skipped and this was not on the list, so the omission was an oversight rather than a decision. Added now as ebrpd-camping-minors at agency scope. The 21-and-over bar is the part worth stating plainly: an 18-year-old may camp unaccompanied but may not be the responsible adult for anyone else.

A STRUCTURAL LIMIT FOUND WHILE MAKING A CAMPGROUND A FIRST-CLASS OBJECTIVE, recorded because it shapes what a campground plan can warn about. Open conflicts are keyed on (permit_group, conflict_id), which is fine for a permit product and useless for land that issues none: every EBRPD conflict this project holds -- chabot-season, chabot-quiet-hours, chabot-overflow-parking and ebrpd-camping-park-count -- sits under the shared 'none' group alongside fifteen trailheads in Plumas, Tahoe, Sequoia, BLM and LTBMU land. So a campground plan CANNOT list the conflicts that bear on it: showing every 'none' conflict would be right today by coincidence of coverage and wrong the first time a Plumas NF disagreement is logged, which is the same reasoning that made jurisdiction an explicit column rather than an inference. NOT WORKED AROUND. Instead the Anthony Chabot row now states the season disagreement in terms the existing scavenger-hunt mechanism already surfaces, so the most trip-blocking fact about that campground -- that it may be closed 1 November to 1 April -- reaches every plan for it rather than only the full --open-questions view. THE REAL FIX, not attempted here, is a scope on a conflict thread the way regulations have one: a conflict about a campground should be keyed to that campground, about an agency to the agency, and about a permit to the permit. That would also let the Desolation and CPMA threads say what they are about rather than which permit they were filed under.

EBRPD's camping page, pasted in full. CORRECTS HOW GROUP AND BACKPACK SITES ARE RELEASED, which this project had recorded as a horizon rather than a mechanism. They go in TWO SIX-MONTH BLOCK RELEASES, not a rolling window: arrival dates July-December 2026 are open now, and January-June 2027 opens for reservation in December 2026. The practical shape is different from what a horizon implies -- a date is unbookable until its block opens however far ahead you plan, and an entire half-year of inventory competes on one morning, by phone only, two reservations per call. The earlier entry recorded 'taking arrival dates through December 2026', which was true and read as a rolling limit. CONFIRMS that family campsites really are on a rolling 12-week window, so the two classes work differently and neither can be read off the other. POINTS AT THE DOCUMENT MOST LIKELY TO SETTLE THE OPEN chabot-season CONFLICT: EBRPD publishes a 'Seasonal and Site Closure List' (PDF) and asks that it be reviewed before calling to inquire. It has NOT been read here and the conflict stays open, but the pointer is recorded on the reservations channel so the next person looking does not start from the brochure and the booking system again. ALSO POINTS AT the Group Campsite Minimums, Maximums and Vehicles table, read separately at none-2026-09-16-03.

Black Diamond Mines Regional Preserve, pasted in full, plus its map and brochure PDFs. A THIRD EBRPD PARK, in Contra Costa County near Antioch -- 8,533 acres, and the first in this project east of the Diablo ridge. ADDS TWO CAMPGROUNDS THAT ARE NOT ALIKE. Star Mine Group Camp is limited to ORGANIZED, EDUCATIONAL GROUPS ONLY, which is a restriction on who may book rather than how many, and the only one of its kind in this project; capacity 35, two-night limit, open all year, picnic tables and a pit toilet, and NO WATER AT THE SITE AT ALL -- campers bring their own and haul their own rubbish out. Stewartville Backpack Camp is open to the general public, holds 20, sits 3.2 miles from the headquarters parking lot near the Stewartville/Upper Oil Canyon junction, and its only water is a NON-POTABLE horse supply, added to water_sources.csv rather than buried in prose. ITS TWO-NIGHT LIMIT IS QUALIFIED 'during the spring, summer, and fall' and what happens in winter is NOT STATED -- recorded as unconfirmed rather than assumed to be the same. A VEHICLE-CAP DISAGREEMENT, small and concrete: this park's page allows a maximum of eight cars at Star Mine while the District's 2026 group camping table caps a 35-capacity site at seven. One car decides whether a party arrives together. A SCHEMA GAP MET HEAD-ON: park gate hours here run in SEVEN SEASONAL BANDS (8am-5pm in deep winter through 8am-8pm in summer) and park_access.csv holds one closing time. The bands are stated verbatim in gate_hours_conditions and gate_close says it varies, because flattening them to one figure would be wrong for most of the year -- and a backpacker walking out 3.2 miles from Stewartville has to clear a gate that shuts at 5pm in November. CONFIRMS THE ESA DISTINCTION from a second park: service animals are allowed on guided underground mine tours and emotional support animals are not, which is the same line Anthony Chabot's booking system drew and is already carried on ebrpd-pets-prohibited-areas. NOT CAPTURED: the Coal Mine Experience programme, Rose Hill Cemetery, the mining and Bay Miwok history, naturalist programmes and the dated event listings -- none of them change a camping plan, and the events are exactly the dated material this schema still cannot hold. The two PDFs are map sheets whose text is labels; nothing was taken from them that the page did not already say.

EBRPD's 2026 Group Camping Minimum, Maximums and Vehicles table. CORRECTS A FIGURE THIS PROJECT CLOSED A CONFLICT ON YESTERDAY AND GOT PARTLY WRONG. ebrpd-group-camp-minimum was closed at 17 people, on three surfaces against one, and 17 is indeed the District's floor -- but it is not the answer for every group camp. The table scales the minimum with capacity: a 300-person site needs 100, a 100-person site needs 50, and 17 applies at 75 and below. So Bort Meadow, at 300, needs a party of 100, and Hawk Ridge and Lost Ridge, at 100, need 50. A group of twenty reading this project yesterday would have believed it could book Bort Meadow. Seven group camp rows corrected. The closed conflict is NOT reopened: the question it settled was whether the District floor is 10 or 17, and that answer stands. This is a different fact the floor was being made to stand in for. ADDS PER-SITE VEHICLE CAPS, which the table names for four sites outright: Bort Meadow 75, Hawk Ridge 25, Puma Point 13, Two Rocks 13, and Del Valle's developed sites 15. ADDS the rules around them -- vehicles park in the lot or area nearest the site, no driving into the campsite on roads or trails, NO ADDITIONAL PARKING PASSES ARE AVAILABLE, and motorhomes, RVs and tent trailers are not permitted at group campsites at all. ADDS that backpack and equestrian capacities and vehicle limits vary by site and are only obtainable by calling Reservations, which is a stated gap rather than one this project can close by reading. HOW THIS WAS READ, STATED BECAUSE IT BOUNDS THE CONFIDENCE: the source is a three-column PDF that extracts as flattened columns, so the tier VALUES are certain and the row-by-row alignment was reconstructed from capacities already confirmed per site. Only the five sites the table names in parentheses are certain as site-to-row matches. Every corrected row says so and points at Reservations.

Black Diamond Mines on ReserveAmerica, pasted in full. ADDS A SCOPE THIS PROJECT DID NOT HAVE, because this park contradicts its own District in a way that would send someone out with the wrong kit. EBRPD's agency-wide fire rule permits portable barbecues and hibachis; Black Diamond permits NO campfires and NO barbecues at any time, camp stoves only. Read at agency scope alone, a planner packs a barbecue they may not use. regulations.csv gains a 'park' scope_type, sitting between permit_group and wilderness in specificity, because that is the direction real strictness runs -- a park unit tightens what its agency allows. Three rules added at that scope: the fire ban, a total alcohol ban (against Anthony Chabot's beer and wine, which is the contrast most likely to catch someone), and haul-out-everything, which pairs with there being no water at Star Mine and only non-potable horse water at Stewartville. SETTLES THE STAR MINE VEHICLE COUNT AT 7. The park page said a maximum of eight cars and the District's group camping table said seven; the booking system issues SEVEN PARKING PASSES, emailed 5-7 days ahead. Passes are the enforcement, so seven is the operative number and the park page is the outlier. CONFIRMS THE TIER DERIVATION THIS PROJECT FLAGGED AS RECONSTRUCTED: Star Mine is stated here as minimum 17, maximum 35, which is exactly what the flattened-column reading of the 2026 table produced for a 35-capacity site. The derivation was right, and the caveat on the other six rows stays, since only this one has been checked against a second source. THE FINDING THAT WOULD HAVE COST A TRIP: STAR MINE IS NOT REACHED FROM BLACK DIAMOND. The booking system sends its parties to 1200 Frederickson Lane -- the Contra Loma entrance, a different park unit -- to park on gravel by the gate before that park's main entrance. Only Stewartville uses Black Diamond's own 5175 Somersville Road entrance. The row's park stays Black Diamond because that is where the campsite lies, but it now says outright that the entrance fee and seven seasonal gate bands resolved against that park are not necessarily what a Star Mine party meets on arrival. Contra Loma's own access is not in this project. TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT INGESTED. The preserve's acreage is given as 8,533 on EBRPD's page and 6,096 here; it gates nothing, so it is recorded in prose without a conflict thread, on the same basis as Anthony Chabot's 20-versus-35-minute drive. And the GPS block is corrupt -- it prints a longitude of -37121.86306, which is not a place -- so no coordinates were taken. CONFIRMS Stewartville's non-potable horse water, stated here as an instruction to bring your own.

Briones Regional Park, pasted in full, with the District camping page re-read alongside it. A FOURTH EBRPD PARK, 6,255 acres in Contra Costa County. NO CAMPGROUND ROWS WERE CREATED, and the reason is the useful part: Briones has three group campsites at 50 to 300 capacity, and this page names NONE of them. A row needs a name; inventing one to fill the gap would assert a facility this project cannot identify. The park_access row records that they exist, so the gap is visible rather than reading as 'Briones has no camping'. Naming them needs the booking system. A NEW SHAPE IN THE DATA, handled rather than forced: a park whose ACCESS is known while nothing in the dataset sits inside it. The referential-integrity join from park_access back to trailheads or campgrounds fails on that, correctly, so Briones is named in a small allowlist with its reason -- dropping the access row until a campsite is named would mean re-reading the park later, and a misspelling still fails the join. THE FEE IS CASH ONLY, and this is the kind of fact that ruins an arrival rather than a plan: Anthony Chabot and Black Diamond both take Visa, MasterCard and Discover, so a reader generalising from either turns up at Briones with a card and cannot pay. SIX SEASONAL GATE BANDS, the second park in two days to need more than one closing time, which strengthens the case that park_access.csv's single gate_close is the wrong shape rather than Black Diamond being unusual. TWO LIMITS RATHER THAN ONE HERE: parking lot hours are 8am to SUNSET, a different constraint from the gate, binding first whenever sunset comes earlier. AND THE BANDS COVER ONLY TWO OF FIVE STAGING AREAS -- Alhambra and Bear Creek are published, Briones Road, Reliez Valley and Lafayette Ridge are not, and whether they follow the same schedule is unconfirmed. SHARPENS A RULE THIS PROJECT ALREADY HELD VAGUELY. Ordinance 38 Attachment C names 'designated sections of Alhambra Creek, Tavan, Diablo View and Orchard Trails in Briones' without saying which sections; this page gives all four precisely, and they are added as a park-scoped pets rule. It matters because Briones is otherwise leash-optional undeveloped land under s.801.3, so these are the exception inside the exception, marked by signage rather than visible on a map. ADDS a navigation hazard worth recording: Briones Road Staging Area is at 2537 Reliez Valley Road and Reliez Valley Staging Area is at 1956 Reliez Valley Road -- different entrances, same road, names that point at each other. Lafayette Ridge has no published address at all. ADDS A BOOKING FACT FROM THE CAMPING PAGE that was not there when it was read yesterday: Reservations often runs very high call volumes, and a BUSY SIGNAL MEANS THE CALL CENTRE IS AT ITS MAXIMUM and you must try again later. The phone channel can refuse you outright, which bites hardest on a block-release morning when it is the only channel open. CONFIRMS the six-month block release and the rolling 12-week family window, unchanged. NOT CAPTURED AS A RULE: the Briones Special Management Area, a 1,600-acre zone restricting trail use by mode and direction and ALTERNATING BICYCLE AND EQUESTRIAN USE ON WEEKENDS BY EVEN AND ODD CALENDAR DAYS. It is real and it changes what a visitor may do, but this project's regulation categories have no concept of trail use, so it is recorded in the park's notes rather than invented into the vocabulary. The same is true of the archery range and the reservable picnic areas, which change no camping plan.

Briones' map brochure, dated 2026/6. NAMES THE THREE GROUP CAMPS THE PARK PAGE ONLY COUNTED: Wee-Ta-Chi, Maud Whalen and Homestead Valley. Rows added, and Briones leaves the allowlist for parks whose access is known while nothing sits in them -- it was there for exactly one commit. AND IT PREVENTS AN ERROR THE MAP ALONE WOULD HAVE CAUSED: the same map labels Oak Grove, Newt Hollow and Crow, which are RESERVABLE PICNIC AREAS, not camps -- Oak Grove 50 and Newt Hollow 150 at Bear Creek, Crow 50 at Alhambra Creek. All six names sit together on the sheet with the same kind of label, and three of them are not campgrounds. TWO FIELDS LEFT BLANK RATHER THAN INFERRED. Access mode: no source says whether you drive to these camps or walk in, and every other EBRPD group camp in this project being drive-in is not evidence about these. Capacity: the park page gives the three together as 50 to 300 and names no per-site figure, which matters more than it looks -- the District's minimum is tiered to capacity, so without a per-site number the minimum party size cannot be resolved either, and a group could be anywhere from 17 to 100 short of being able to book. Both blanks are stated in the rows and held by named test exceptions, so a new blank still fails. CONFIRMS THE LEASH SEGMENTS VERBATIM, word for word as the park page gave them, which matters because that rule was added yesterday at park scope on a single source; it now has two. EXTENDS THE EBMUD PERMIT'S REACH: the brochure marks the EBMUD Briones Reservoir land on the park's western edge 'EBMUD Trail Use Permit required', so it is not only the Chabot-to-Garin trail. CONFIRMS the Briones Special Management Area wording and the five staging areas. NOT CAPTURED: the trail-type key (hiker only, biker only, hiker/biker, hiker/horse), which is the Special Management Area's substance and still has no category in this project's vocabulary.

HOW FAR AHEAD A BRIONES GROUP CAMP MUST BE BOOKED HAS TWO ANSWERS. The park's map brochure, dated 2026/6, says the three group camping areas 'must be reserved at least five business days in advance'. Every other EBRPD surface says three: the Anthony Chabot brochure, the park pages, the District camping page and the booking system all give three business days for group campsites, and booking_channels.csv carries three as the agency-wide figure. IT DECIDES A BOOKING RATHER THAN A DETAIL: a party calling on a Tuesday for the following Monday clears three business days and fails five. TWO READINGS, NEITHER STATED. Briones may simply require longer than the District floor, the way its cash-only kiosk departs from the District's card handling -- in which case the brochure is right and the agency-wide three is wrong here. Or the brochure is stale, though at 2026/6 it is the NEWEST document in this comparison, which cuts against that reading and is why newer-source-wins cannot settle it. The agency-wide three is left as the stored answer because it is what four surfaces say, and the five is recorded on all three Briones rows so nobody books on three without seeing it. Resolving it needs Reservations on (888) 327-2757 option 2.

Briones on ReserveAmerica, overview and campsite listing. FILLS BOTH BLANKS THIS PROJECT LEFT YESTERDAY, and they turn out to matter more than a missing number usually does. Per-site minimums and maximums are stated outright: Wee-Ta-Chi 17-50, Maud Whalen 25-75, Homestead Valley 100-300. The park page had given only '50 to 300' across all three, and because the District's minimum is tiered to capacity, no per-site capacity meant no resolvable minimum either. A party of twenty can book Wee-Ta-Chi, cannot book Maud Whalen, and is eighty short of Homestead Valley -- three different answers the row could not previously give. Access mode stays blank: still nothing said. IT ALSO TESTED THE TIER TABLE THIS PROJECT RECONSTRUCTED FROM A FLATTENED PDF, AND FOUND A ROW OF IT WRONG. Maud Whalen is minimum 25 at 75 capacity; the reconstruction gave 17 for a 75-capacity site. Re-reading the extraction, the '25' placed at the end of the maximum column is really the fifth value of the minimum column, making the table 300/100, 100/50, 75/25, 50/17, 35/17 -- which fits all three stated Briones pairs. NO ANTHONY CHABOT FIGURE RESTED ON THE BAD ROW, because no camp there is 75 capacity, and the four tiers those corrections did use are each now corroborated by a directly stated site. The caveat carried on those rows was the right call and is sharpened rather than removed. ADDS A SEASONAL CLOSURE, 1 NOVEMBER TO 15 MAY: the listing shows Briones open through 31 October 2026 and the park's own text says the group areas are reservable 'beginning May through October'. Nothing read contradicts it, unlike Anthony Chabot's. REFINES THE FAMILY STAY LIMIT in a way the campground rows did not carry: 15 consecutive and 30 total nights are counted PER HOUSEHOLD ADDRESS, customer name, primary occupant or registered vehicle -- not per person -- and walk-in and drop-in stays count toward it. CONFIRMS beer and wine are allowed here with a separate permit for group sites, which is the District norm and shows Black Diamond's total ban to be the park-scoped exception it was recorded as. The GPS on this page is valid, unlike Black Diamond's; no coordinate column exists on campgrounds or park_access, so it was not stored.

CLOSES briones-group-lead-time AT 3 DAYS. The booking system states 'Reservations cannot be made less than 3 days from arrival date' in its facilities text and '3 days in advance' in its alert banner, agreeing with the park page, the District camping page, the Anthony Chabot brochure and booking_channels.csv. That is five surfaces against the Briones map brochure's 'at least five business days'. THE AWKWARD PART IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: the brochure is dated 2026/6 and is the NEWEST document in the comparison, so this closes AGAINST recency, on weight of agreement and on the booking system being the thing that actually refuses a late call. Why the brochure says five is unexplained -- it may be stale despite its date, or a Briones-specific practice that the reservation system does not encode. Three is stored; the five stays recorded on all three Briones rows, so a party working from the printed brochure is not silently contradicted.

EVIDENCE ON chabot-season FROM A SECOND PARK, strengthening it without closing it. Briones' three group camps are seasonally closed 1 November to 15 May, stated plainly by the booking system with no contradicting source. That EBRPD closes camping over the winter at another park, on almost the same calendar Anthony Chabot's disputed closure claims (1 November to 1 April), makes the booking system's Chabot statement look like the District's normal practice rather than an error, and the brochure's flat 'year-round camping is available' look more like the outlier. IT IS STILL NOT DECISIVE, and the reasons are worth stating so nobody treats this as closed: different park, different site class -- Briones' are primitive group camps and Chabot's is a developed family campground with flush toilets and hookups, which is exactly the kind of site a District might keep open through winter. The Chabot closure stays stored as live and the conflict stays open. The Seasonal and Site Closure List named on the camping page remains the document that would settle it.

Black Diamond's per-site booking pages for Stewartville and Star Mine, the deepest level ReserveAmerica publishes. CORRECTS THIS PROJECT'S ACCESS TAG FOR STAR MINE from drive-in to HIKE-IN. The booking system classifies it Hike-In and puts its seven parking spaces a QUARTER MILE from the site; the park page's 'parking available at the site' was read as unloading at the pitch, which it is not. A group of up to 35 carries its kit that far. It also breaks an assumption this project had hardened into a test -- that group camps are driven to -- so the invariant now holds for backpack and family sites and only requires a group camp to state some mode. SETTLES STEWARTVILLE'S WINTER, which this row carried as unconfirmed: the park page limited camping to two nights 'during the spring, summer, and fall' and said nothing about winter, and the listing states a seasonal closure of 1 NOVEMBER TO 31 MARCH. Black Diamond itself stays open through 31 December 2026; only the site shuts. NARROWS WHO MAY BOOK STAR MINE from the park page's 'organized, educational groups' to 'ONLY FOR USE BY SCHOOL GROUPS AND SCOUTS'. A community or church group reading the park page as permission would be refused, and that is a booking-time refusal rather than a gate-time one. ADDS AN ARRIVAL RULE with teeth: at Star Mine ALL VEHICLES MUST ENTER AND EXIT TOGETHER, NO SHUTTLING, and violators may be cited or towed -- a party trickling in across an afternoon is breaking the terms. ADDS check-in 2pm and check-out 12pm for both sites, previously blank. ADDS Stewartville's minimum of 1 person, so a solo camper can book a site this project described only by its capacity of 20. CONFIRMS Star Mine's 7 vehicles, its 17-35 capacity, the Fredrickson Lane access by the Contra Loma entrance, the security deposit, and the no-water, no-fire, no-alcohol terms. ADDS site furniture: Star Mine has a shade structure and 2 tent pads; Stewartville has pole tethering and pipe rails for horses. ONE THING NOTED AND NOT ASSERTED: the listing marks Stewartville 'Pets Allowed: Domestic, Horse' and marks Star Mine with nothing. An absent marker is not a stated ban, and the two sit on one page, so the contrast is recorded in the row as a question for Reservations rather than written in as a prohibition.

HOW MANY VEHICLES MAY A STEWARTVILLE PARTY BRING? Its own booking page answers twice and differently: the structured site detail says 'Maximum Number of Vehicles: 1', while the free-text notes on the same page say 'PARKING: 5 parking passes'. Internal, so the page has discredited itself and no ranking of publishers helps. IT DECIDES WHETHER A GROUP CAN GO AT ALL: the site holds up to 20 people and sits 3.2 miles from the trailhead, so a party of eight arriving in three cars is either fine or four vehicles over. Both readings are plausible -- 1 may be a default the District never set for a backpack site, or 5 may be copied from a template -- and neither is stated. Neither figure is stored as the answer; both are in the row. Resolving it needs Reservations on (888) 327-2757 option 2, or the information letter EBRPD emails 5-7 days before arrival, which carries the parking passes themselves and would settle it by counting them.

Anthony Chabot's campsite listing, pasted a second time. IT IS THE SAME LISTING, and that was checked rather than assumed: the loops were re-derived from this paste independently of what is stored and every count matches -- 9 in Loop C, 26 in Loop D, 13 in Loop F, with 006 and 022 present -- and the six sites absent from the listing are the same six, 010, 031, 033, 039, 053 and 075. All six named group camps carry the same capacities and the same Seasonal A and B designations. Nothing drifted. RE-READING IT STILL FOUND A GAP, the second time in three days a duplicate has. When Briones' booking page was read yesterday it stated that the family stay limit is counted PER HOUSEHOLD ADDRESS, customer name, primary occupant or registered vehicle rather than per person, and that walk-in and drop-in stays count toward the tally. That was written into the log entry and never into ebrpd-camping-stay-limit, which is the agency-wide rule that states the limit -- so the fact was recorded as provenance without ever becoming an answer, which is the failure this project's own logging discipline is meant to prevent. It is the same shape as the juveniles rule missed on 2026-09-15. Added to the rule's detail now. IT MATTERS: a family reading '30 total days per year' as a per-person allowance plans roughly twice the camping it may actually book, and cannot fix it by reserving in another member's name. THE PATTERN IS WORTH NAMING: both misses happened when a fact arrived inside a block of text about something else -- the juveniles rule inside group camping, this inside a Briones page -- and was summarised rather than filed. Re-reading duplicates is how they surface.

EBRPD's Alerts and Closures page, pasted in full -- roughly sixty live notices across the District. MOST OF IT THIS PROJECT STILL CANNOT HOLD, and this is the clearest instance yet of the gap the scorecard reports as 'What is closed?' no-model for all 462 objectives: trail closures at Anthony Chabot, Briones, Sunol, Morgan Territory, Round Valley and Contra Loma, blue-green algae advisories at Lake Chabot and both Del Valle swim beaches, a golden mussel quarantine affecting Del Valle, Lake Chabot, Quarry Lakes and Shadow Cliffs, and a boil-water advisory at Piedmont Stables. Every one is dated and every one expires; there is nowhere to put a fact with an end. THREE THINGS DID FIT THE SCHEMA, and they are the reason to read an alerts page rather than skip it. FIRST, A DATED OFFICIAL WATER CHECK of the whole Ohlone corridor: Eagle Springs, Backpack Camp, Doe Camp, Maggie's Half Acre, Boyd Camp, Stromer Springs and Stewart's Camp all listed as water available on 2026-09-15, with EBRPD restating that ALL of it is non-potable. Seven ledger entries added. It is the newest check on Boyd Camp, where an official update and this project's own field note have disagreed since 2026-09-04 -- it does not disprove the field note and both older entries stay, but it is now what the latest-status view reports. It is also the first official update to cover Stromer Springs, which this project held only on a maintainer's in-person report. EBRPD wrote one entry as 'Backpack Camp' with no park name; mapped to Sunol Backpack Camp, which is the corridor camp the rest of the list covers. SECOND, A PARK-SCOPED FIRE BAN AT SUNOL, stricter than Black Diamond's: no open fires or barbecues of any type, and gas stoves permitted at Alameda Grove and School Camp ONLY -- neither of which is Sunol Backpack Camp, the camp this project actually holds. The District's agency rule permits portable barbecues, so a backpacker planning a hot meal there on that basis plans something they may not do. It is posted as a fire warning rather than in the camping text, and whether it lifts outside fire season is not stated; recorded as standing because its exceptions are named by place rather than by date. THIRD, A CAMPGROUND THIS PROJECT DID NOT HAVE, arriving through its own outage: Round Valley Backpack Camp, whose water supply is not working until further notice. The row is deliberately thin -- no capacity, fee, restroom, reservation terms or season, because no source read states them -- and it carries the fact that Ordinance 38 Attachment B prohibits dogs in the whole of Round Valley Regional Preserve as a wildlife protection area, which is a harder bar than any leash rule and reaches the camp.

ADDS data/advisories.csv, and with it the first answer this project has ever had for the scorecard's 'What is closed?', which has read no-model for all 462 objectives since the scorecard existed. Eight advisories from EBRPD's alerts page, scoped to the five parks this project actually holds. WHAT MAKES THIS TABLE DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER ONE HERE: an advisory is a fact with an end. A permit quota, a leash rule and a campground fee stay true until someone corrects them; a trail is closed until the culvert is repaired. Storing the second kind the way this project stores the first would produce exactly what it exists to prevent -- a closure read in September and repeated in March is not stale data, it is a wrong answer with a date on it. THREE PROPERTIES ARE STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CONVENTION. An advisory with no observed_date is REFUSED AT LOAD, because the date is the only thing that lets a reader judge the rest. An end date and until_further_notice cannot both be set, because they are the two answers the table exists to keep apart, and a row claiming both is refused too. And an open-ended advisory NEVER expires on its own: the agency has not said it is over, and deciding that for them is the failure mode. Instead its age is reported, and past 30 days it is flagged as old enough to doubt -- not a claim about how long closures last, but how long this project is willing to repeat one without saying when it last looked. Storm damage is repaired in a fortnight and an algae bloom clears faster. plan resolves advisories by DATE as well as scope, so a trip planned after a stated reopening is not warned about a closure that will be over, and prints them ABOVE cost and facilities, because a closed trail changes whether the trip happens where a fee only changes what it costs. WHAT WAS NOT ADDED, and why. Sunol's fire warning stayed a park-scoped REGULATION rather than becoming an advisory: its exceptions are named by place, not by date, and holding one fact in two tables is the drift the regulations table was built to stop. Round Valley's water outage stayed in the water ledger, which already records dated checks and is the right home. Advisories at Contra Loma and Lake Chabot were left out because neither park has a row here for them to attach to -- Contra Loma matters, since Star Mine parties park there, and that gap is recorded rather than papered over by scoping its notice to a park it is not in. The golden mussel quarantine IS recorded against Del Valle, because the quarantine bites at Del Valle even though the detection was at Contra Loma. ONE ADVISORY IS NOT REALLY ONE: Anthony Chabot's Bird Trail re-route is permanent, not a condition, but EBRPD publishes it among the alerts and it will never expire; it is kept with that said in its detail, because a map printed before August 2025 shows a loop that is not there.

Round Valley's park page and all three of its ReserveAmerica pages. FILLS THE THINNEST ROW IN THIS PROJECT: the camp entered a day ago through a water-outage notice with a name, a park and nothing else. It now has capacity 1-25, check-in 2pm, check-out 12pm, graded tent pads, a picnic table, hitching rails, two vehicles, and an ADA-ACCESSIBLE VAULT TOILET -- so has_restroom was corrected from False, where it had been a default that could be misread as 'there is no toilet'. RECONCILES THREE SOURCES THAT LOOK LIKE THEY DISAGREE ABOUT WATER. The park page says non-potable water is available at the site; the booking system says NO WATER, bring all you need; the alerts page says the supply is not working until further notice. All three are true at once: the supply exists, it is non-potable, and it is currently broken. The park page describes the normal state and the booking system the current one. This also CONFIRMS a value stored yesterday on no evidence -- potability was set False as the conservative reading, and the park page states it. THE WALK IS 3.4 OR 3.6 MILES: the booking system gives 18,000 feet, which is 3.41, and the park page says 3.6. Recorded as both without a conflict thread, because neither gates a decision at that margin -- though for a party carrying every litre of its own water to a site EBRPD warns commonly exceeds 100F, the longer figure is the one to plan on. FOUR RULES ADDED, THREE OF WHICH REACH CAMPS THIS PROJECT ALREADY HELD. The District treats BACKPACK SITES as their own class and publishes their terms only through the booking system: a 2-night stay limit, except on the Ohlone Wilderness Trail where 3 consecutive nights are allowed because the trail is 28 miles and two nights does not cover it; no campfires or charcoal barbecues, camp stoves only; and NO ALCOHOL AT ALL, beer and wine included, where the family campgrounds permit both. Each is stricter than the Ordinance 38 rule it sits under, and each reaches Boyd, Stewart's, Maggie's Half Acre, Doe, Sunol Backpack, Eagle Springs and Round Valley. NO DOGS OVERNIGHT at the Mission Peak, Sunol and Ohlone Trail backpack sites is scoped to the AGENCY rather than a park, deliberately: those camps are filed under Del Valle Regional Park, where the family campground allows dogs, so a park-scoped rule would ban them at the wrong campground. It is an overnight ban rather than a leash requirement -- a dog may walk the trail and may not sleep at the camp -- and whether it reaches a cat is NOT STATED, unlike Ordinance 38's own 'dog, cat, or other animal' wording. ROUND VALLEY BANS DOGS ENTIRELY, park-wide, and the page gives the cause: the endangered San Joaquin kit fox is here at the northern extreme of its range and dogs are a disease vector to it. Attachment B listed the preserve without saying why. ADDS THE HALF OF Q8 THIS PROJECT CALLED UNANSWERABLE FOUR COMMITS AGO. 'Can I change or cancel, AND BY WHEN' had a channel and no cutoff; backpack sites have both -- two days before arrival, by phone, up to 4pm, with an $8 cancellation fee and a separate $8 non-refundable change fee on top of a non-refundable $8 reservation fee. A cancelled backpack trip costs $16 before any nightly rate. AND NO REFUNDS for inclement weather, stricter fire restrictions or water quality issues -- the three things most likely to stop the trip are the three EBRPD will not refund. ADDS a park_access row with six seasonal gate bands, the third park here to need more than one closing time, and free parking.

Coyote Hills' park page and both its map PDFs. ADDS DAIRY GLEN GROUP CAMP: capacity 50, three shade structures, picnic tables, a drinking fountain, A FIRE PIT, a hand-washing station and vault toilets, reservable 3 or more business days ahead. FULLY ADA COMPLIANT after a Regional Parks Foundation renovation, with a hardened path to the shade structures -- the only campground in this project described as accessible rather than merely having an accessible toilet. THE FIRE PIT IS NOTABLE AGAINST THE REST OF THE DATASET: every EBRPD backpack site bans fires outright and Black Diamond bans them park-wide, so a provided pit is the exception, and Ordinance 38 s.404's 'only in the facilities provided' is what governs it. ADDS THE FIRST POTABLE WATER SOURCE HERE. Every other source in this project is a spigot or trough EBRPD states is non-potable; this is described as a drinking fountain at a renovated camp. Recorded potable as the reading, with the caveat that no page says the word. THE GATE SCHEMA BREAKS PROPERLY FOR THE FIRST TIME. Black Diamond, Briones and Round Valley each need multiple closing times but open at 8am in every band, so gate_open held one storable figure. Coyote Hills opens at 7am for five months and 8am for seven, so both ends now say 'varies by season'. That is four parks in three days whose hours this schema cannot express, and the single gate_open/gate_close pair is now clearly the wrong shape rather than an awkward fit. ADDS A CONCEPT NO PARK HAD: a PARK CURFEW of 10pm-5am, distinct from the gate. The gate governs vehicle entry; the curfew governs being in the park at all, and between gate close and 10pm the two differ. ADDS that the waters west and south are the Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge, run by U.S. Fish and Wildlife -- a fourth agency touching this project's parks, whose land is not held here, and where DOGS ARE NOT ALLOWED even though Coyote Hills permits them. NOT CAPTURED: the Visitor Center's holiday schedule, the Nectar Garden, naturalist programmes and the Ohlone exhibits -- none change a camping plan.

EVIDENCE ON THE 15-VERSUS-18 PARK COUNT, AND ONE OF THE THREE CANDIDATE EXPLANATIONS IS NOW SETTLED. When that conflict was opened, three readings were offered for the gap of three: the finder tagging a park whose camping Reservations does not handle, Dumbarton Quarry being counted separately while sitting inside Coyote Hills, and Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer being one paired parkland with two entries. DUMBARTON IS CONFIRMED AS A CAMPGROUND OF COYOTE HILLS, not a park. Coyote Hills' own map brochure lists it under that park's Camping heading beside Dairy Glen -- 'The Dairy Glen area is available for group overnight camping. Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay offers tent, car, and RV camping' -- which agrees with ReserveAmerica's 'located within Coyote Hills Regional Park'. The park finder lists it separately, but a finder entry is a navigation choice rather than a claim about boundaries. So 18 finder entries contain at least one campground counted as a park, and the gap is at most two. THE CONFLICT STAYS OPEN because that is not the whole gap: Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer are untested, and so is whether the Tilden trio -- Regional Park, Nature Area and Botanic Garden -- is one park or three. THE ROW CHANGE CARRIES A CAUTION rather than a clean win: with park set to Coyote Hills, Dumbarton now inherits that park's $5 parking and six seasonal gate bands, and Dumbarton has its own entrance on the Bay side and its own brochure. Whether a Dumbarton camper meets Coyote Hills' gate and fee is unconfirmed -- the same shape as Star Mine, which lies in Black Diamond and is entered from Contra Loma.

Coyote Hills' three ReserveAmerica pages -- overview, campsites list and Dairy Glen's own booking page. CORRECTS DAIRY GLEN FROM DRIVE-IN TO HIKE-IN, and this is the worse of the two access corrections made in two days. Star Mine's drive_in at least came from a page saying parking was available at the site. Dairy Glen's came from nothing: no source read yesterday said how you reach it, and drive_in was written because a group camp with shade structures and a stone BBQ sounded like somewhere you park.
