The listing says it twice -- 'This is a HIKE-IN only site (approximately 1/4 mile on a flat, paved surface)' and 'Hike-in ONLY site. NO vehicle access (driving into/out of site)' -- so up to fifty people carry their kit a quarter mile while their ten permitted vehicles stay at the lot. THE LESSON IS NOT ABOUT ACCESS MODE. It is that a blank field and a guessed field render identically to a reader, and this schema already has the rule for it: absent is not a value. access_mode blank prints 'access mode not recorded'. Writing drive_in turned a gap into a claim, and nothing downstream could tell the difference. Any field filled without a source should have been left blank. CONFIRMS THE MINIMUM PARTY SIZE THAT WAS RECORDED AS NOT STATED: minimum 17, maximum 50. Yesterday's row said no page gave a minimum, derived 17 from the District's 2026 tier table, and warned that the table's row alignment had been reconstructed and found wrong in one place. The derivation was right. That is one hit and not a rehabilitation -- the row known to be wrong is still wrong, and the caveat stays on every other figure taken from that table. FILLS: check-in 2pm, check-out 12pm, maximum 10 vehicles, security deposit required, open year-round, and an ADA Accessible flag from the booking system that now agrees with the park page's fully-ADA-compliant claim -- the quarter mile being flat and paved is what lets both be true at once. Fuller facilities than the park page gave: three shade structures, three 20ft picnic tables, a 6ft stone BBQ, a drinking fountain, a fire circle with benches, a hand-washing station and vault toilets. PETS ALLOWED: DOMESTIC is stated, where Star Mine's listing leaves the field blank -- two EBRPD group camps, one marked and one not, which makes the Star Mine omission a pattern worth asking about rather than a slip. ADDS THE FIRST PARK-SCOPED BOOKING CHANNEL, coyote-hills-group, and with it a park argument to booking.channels_for that did not exist: booking mechanics have been agency-wide since the table was built, and a park-scoped row would have loaded and resolved to nothing. Dairy Glen's page states 'Reservations must be completed and paid in full 5 working days prior to your arrival date or 3 days prior if picking up parking passes/permits', against the District's 3 days. Five working days is the figure to plan on; the three-day version here is the shorter deadline for a party collecting passes, and read carelessly it looks like the District figure. 'Paid in full' is new wording nothing else in that table carries. SCOPE IS A JUDGEMENT: the sentence was read on one site's page, and is stored at park scope because Star Mine, Stewartville, Briones and Round Valley do not carry it. If another Coyote Hills camp turns up without it, the row belongs at site scope, which this schema does not have. NOT CAPTURED: the acreage disagreement and the coordinates went into the park access row as prose -- 1,266 acres on the park page against 978 here, no conflict thread because neither changes a plan, and 37.5575/-122.08583 in prose because no table in this project has a coordinates field. ONE CODE FIX THE QUOTE FORCED: open_questions flags a row uncertain when its notes contain 'approximate', 'unconfirmed' and two other markers. Quoting ReserveAmerica's 'approximately 1/4 mile on a flat, paved surface' tripped it, and the report asked a visitor to go and confirm a distance the operator had already stated. The markers exist to catch THIS PROJECT hedging, not a source hedging, so a quoted span is now stripped before they are matched. Across all committed data the open-question list is unchanged, 85 before and after, so no existing flag depended on a marker sitting inside a quotation.

EVIDENCE AGAINST YESTERDAY'S RESOLUTION, FILED THE DAY AFTER IT WAS MADE. Entry -18 closed one of the three candidate explanations for the 15-versus-18 camping park count by resolving Dumbarton Quarry Campground's park field to Coyote Hills. This page, ReserveAmerica's own listing for Coyote Hills, says 'Dumbarton Quarry and Ardenwood Historic Farm parks are located nearby' -- calling Dumbarton a PARK, and placing it NEARBY rather than inside. It lines up with EBRPD's park finder, which lists Dumbarton as a park in its own right, and against the Coyote Hills brochure, which lists the campground under its own Camping heading. The reading is now 2-2 across sources rather than 2-1. THE RESOLUTION IS LEFT STANDING, and the reason is worth stating so it can be argued with: a brochure listing a campground under a park's Camping heading is a claim about what is in the park, while a sentence pointing visitors at what else is around is a claim about convenience, and 'nearby' is what anyone would write about a camp with its own entrance several miles round the marsh even if the boundary enclosed it. But this is now a live disagreement rather than a settled question, so the thread stays open and the caution on the campground row -- that it inherits Coyote Hills' $5 parking and six seasonal gate bands while having its own entrance, exactly the Star Mine shape -- matters more, not less. What would settle it is a boundary map or the District's own statement of which park the campground lies in; neither has been read here.

Garin's park page. ADDS GARIN REGIONAL PARK and Arroyo Flats Group Camp, and ADDS A CLOSURE: Dry Creek Garden is shut until further notice for storm damage, the fourth storm closure in the advisories table. SIX GATE BANDS THAT DO NOT COVER THE YEAR. Nov 1-Mar 5 8am-6pm; Mar 6-Apr 16 8am-7pm; Apr 17-May 21 8am-8pm; May 22-Aug 27 8am-9pm; Aug 28-Sep 24 8am-8pm; Sep 25-Oct 29 8am-7pm. OCTOBER 30 AND 31 FALL IN NO BAND. The last band ends Oct 29 and the next begins Nov 1, and the two neighbouring bands differ by an hour, so a party arriving on Halloween has no published closing time to check -- at a park whose group camp instructs them to check exactly that. Recorded as a gap in the source rather than a closure. This is the fifth park in four days whose hours the single gate_open/gate_close pair cannot express, and the first whose published bands are also incomplete; park_hours.csv would have to model a gap, not just a band. Opening is 8am throughout, so that figure is storable. Garin's 9pm summer close is the latest in this project. CASH ONLY, the second such park after Briones, against Coyote Hills one park over taking tap to pay -- payment method is a per-park fact in this District and does not carry. Fee charged only when the kiosk is attended, the same unresolved wording Black Diamond and Briones have: nothing says what happens when it is not. TWO ADDRESSES ON ONE ROAD: the park page gives 1580 Garin Avenue, ReserveAmerica gives the group site and the park's mailing address as 1320 Garin Avenue. Both are EBRPD's. Recorded, not resolved -- a party at the wrong number is at least on the right road. NOT CAPTURED: the Apple Festival, the Red Barn's blacksmith and tool shops, and the Edith Meyers passage, none of which change a plan. The cattle warning went into the park notes because it is addressed to dog owners and this project holds a dog-owning reader.

Garin's three ReserveAmerica pages. SEVEN AGENCY-WIDE RULES THAT HAVE BEEN ON EVERY EBRPD LISTING READ FOR THIS PROJECT AND WERE NEVER FILED. The 'Additional Information' block appears on Anthony Chabot's, Black Diamond's, Briones', Round Valley's and Coyote Hills' pages as well as this one. Parts of it were taken -- the per-household stay counting, the emotional-support-animal line, the minors rule -- and the rest was read past. This is the same failure named twice before in this log: a fact arriving inside text about something else gets summarised in a log entry and never becomes a row. The Briones entry, none-2026-09-16-08, literally says 'CONFIRMS beer and wine are allowed here with a separate permit for group sites' and no alcohol rule existed in regulations.csv until today. ADDED: no hard alcohol, beer and wine only at campsites and picnic areas, and a group campsite needing an additional beer-and-wine permit bought in advance -- now with the first price this project has for it, $25.00 from Arroyo Flats' own page. Firewood must be commercially purchased, processed logs or cut lumber and COLLECTING IS PROHIBITED, which is the supply half of the fire question and separate from whether a fire is allowed. No smoking or vaping. Tents unlimited in number but only on dirt or designated pads, never on lawns -- ground, not count, is the binding constraint. Two vehicles per family campsite, with group and backpack sites stating their own (and none of the three read here matches: 7, 10, 15). A maximum of two family campsites per household on any date, additional ones CANCELLED, one per date for other site types, and groups over 16 directed to a group site. Maximum three dogs per site, confined to a vehicle or tent during quiet hours. ONE OF THOSE IS WRITTEN ABOUT DOGS WHERE ORDINANCE 38 IS WRITTEN ABOUT ANIMALS, and it is the count. Three dogs per site is stated; no number is given for cats or other animals, and reading the dog figure across would be inventing one. ALSO ADDS to the group booking channel that a cabin, group, backpack or equestrian reservation gets an information letter emailed 5-7 days ahead. That is not a courtesy note -- at Arroyo Flats it carries the combination to the group site's locked gate, and that site's own page says 5-10 days instead of 5-7. ONE SCHEMA LIMIT THIS EXPOSED AND DID NOT FIX: fee_status reads a row's fee text and returns charges, free or unknown. Arroyo Flats has NO nightly rate on file and a stated $25 alcohol permit, so the row reports as charging and the cost header says the trip is not free -- both true, and neither says the site's price is unknown. This is the same shape the cpma permit already has, free for the permit and $5.00 a day for the parking, so it is a known and accepted pattern rather than a new bug. The fee text now leads with this project's own guard, 'absent is not free', so the component line carries the warning whatever the header counts. A per-item fee model would fix it properly and is not built. AND THE OPEN-QUESTION LIST IMMEDIATELY OBJECTED, correctly: the count of EBRPD rules citing ReserveAmerica went from 3 to 10, and that question exists because a booking vendor does not own what you may do on the land. The objection is right and the rules are still worth having -- these are the terms every EBRPD reservation is made under, published by EBRPD through its own system, not ReserveAmerica's invention. But none of them carries an Ordinance 38 citation, and the generators thread is what that gap looks like when it bites. Tracing these seven back to the ordinance, or establishing that the ordinance does not contain them, is the follow-up.

ARROYO FLATS' MINIMUM PARTY SIZE, contradicted by two EBRPD pages read on the same day. The booking system says it twice -- 'Minimum Number of People 17' in the site details and 'CAPACITY: minimum 17, maximum 75' in the site note. The park page says the site 'can accommodate groups of 25 people or more, up to 75'. Maximum 75 is agreed; the floor is not. WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A TYPO: 25 is what the District's capacity tier table gives for a 75-capacity site. That table was reconstructed here from a flattened PDF, found wrong in one row at Briones, and corrected to 300/100, 100/50, 75/25, 50/17, 35/17 against three directly stated Briones pairs -- one of which, Maud Whalen, is 25 at 75 capacity, exactly Arroyo Flats' shape. So the park page agrees with the tier table and with the one other 75-capacity site on file, and the booking system disagrees with all three. AND YET THE BOOKING SYSTEM IS NOT SIMPLY WRONG, because yesterday it was right: Dairy Glen's minimum was 17 at 50 capacity, which the tier table also predicted, and the booking system is the only place either figure is stated as a number rather than derived. NOT RESOLVED, AND THE CHANNEL IS WHY IT MATTERS. Group sites are booked BY PHONE, so no online checkout enforces the 17; whatever figure the Reservations agent applies is the one that decides whether a party of twenty gets the site. A party of 17 to 24 should call and ask before planning on either number. A party of 25 or more is safe under both.

GENERATORS: THE ORDINANCE AND THE BOOKING TERMS DISAGREE, and both are EBRPD. Ordinance 38 s.400.2 and s.908.2 set a DISTURBANCE TEST -- no generator or sound-amplification device may be operated in a campground if it disturbs other campers -- which permits a quiet one at any hour, and is how this project has recorded it since the ordinance was ingested. The campground rules attached to every EBRPD reservation say 'No gas generators', flat, with no condition. A camper reading the ordinance brings one. A camper reading the terms they agreed to at booking does not. LEFT UNRESOLVED, with the safer reading named in the rule: the booking rules are the terms the reservation is made under, so plan on the flat ban -- but that is a judgement about which document governs, not something either document says. ONE DETAIL WORTH KEEPING: the booking rules ban GAS generators specifically, while the ordinance names no fuel. A battery power station may sit outside both, and nothing read says so either way, so it is a question rather than an answer.

THE THIRD CANDIDATE EXPLANATION FOR THE 15-VERSUS-18 CAMPING PARK COUNT IS NOW EVIDENCED, which leaves one of the three untested. When that conflict was opened, the gap of three had three offered readings: the park finder tagging a park whose camping Reservations does not handle; Dumbarton Quarry being counted separately while sitting inside Coyote Hills; and Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer being one parkland with two finder entries. THE THIRD IS NOW SOURCED. EBRPD's own page calls them 'two adjoining parks from former 19th Century ranches' and gives a combined figure -- over 5,800 acres and more than 35 miles of trails -- for the pair rather than for either. ReserveAmerica says Garin 'shares a contiguous border with sister park Dry Creek Pioneer Regional Park'. The camping is at Garin: Arroyo Flats is the only camp either page names, and nothing read gives Dry Creek Pioneer a camp of its own. So the finder can list two parks where Reservations has one camping park. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO TO THE COUNT. Two of three explanations now have evidence -- this one, and Dumbarton at entry -18, which the very next source argued against and which stands at 2-2. Taken at face value they account for two of the three, leaving one unexplained. That is not a resolution and the thread stays open: neither explanation has been confirmed by EBRPD saying so, both are this project reading its own sources, and the remaining one is the reading nothing has tested. The honest state is a gap of one that nobody here has looked for.

Briones' three per-site booking pages, one for each group camp. CORRECTS ALL THREE FROM DRIVE-IN TO HIKE-IN and closes report R0002, the only access_mode in this dataset that rested on no document. It was stored flagged, filed as a report, and it took one page to settle -- which is the case for storing an unsourced value visibly rather than quietly. THE REPORT WAS NOT SIMPLY WRONG, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART. Wee-Ta-Chi's own note says driving to the site IS permitted, four vehicles, conditions permitting -- and is forbidden when raining or when trails have been wet WITHIN SEVEN DAYS. So the site is drive-in in dry weather and a 1.5-MILE CARRY otherwise, six times the quarter-mile at Star Mine, Dairy Glen and Arroyo Flats, and which one a party gets depends on rain in the preceding week rather than on the forecast for their dates. access_mode holds one value; EBRPD's own field says Hike-In, which is the half a party must be able to do. A SCHEMA GAP, then, not a bad report: nothing here can express an access mode conditional on antecedent weather. Homestead Valley and Maud Whalen publish no site notes, so for those two hike-in is all any source says. ALCOHOL IS NOT PERMITTED AT WEE-TA-CHI, stated on its page, which contradicts what this project recorded for Briones yesterday and what it filed District-wide today. It is NOT in regulations.csv because that table's narrowest scope is PARK and this is published for one site, while Briones' other two publish nothing -- so it went on the campground row and the agency rule names it as an exception with nowhere to go. That is the second schema gap this one page opened. A REFUND THE DISTRICT OTHERWISE REFUSES: 'IF TRAILS ARE WET, THEY ARE CLOSED TO ALL TRAFFIC. If this means you must cancel your event, call Reservations for a refund or to reschedule.' EBRPD's backpack cancellation terms, already recorded, state no refunds for inclement weather of any kind. Wet trails at Wee-Ta-Chi are explicitly refundable. Driving on closed trails costs future access to sites and a repair bill. NO WATER AT WEE-TA-CHI, stated outright -- so the absence is the fact and no water_sources row is created for it. ALSO FILLS on all three: check-in 2pm, check-out 12pm, security deposit, Pets Allowed Domestic, vehicle counts of 10, 15 and 35, and a QUIET AREA flag none of the other EBRPD group camps read here carries. Maud Whalen adds a LEAN TO/SHELTER and a PLATFORM, both unique in this dataset. Homestead Valley's list is shorter than its neighbours' -- no BBQ flag, no shade rating, no ADA -- which is recorded as a contrast rather than as a stated absence. CONFIRMS THE SEASONAL CLOSURE from a fourth surface: all three loops are named 'Primitive Group Camp Seasonal'. Every date on all three calendars reads Call Center, confirming group sites are not sold online. AND IT WEAKENS YESTERDAY'S SCOPE ARGUMENT FOR COYOTE HILLS' FIVE-WORKING-DAY DEADLINE. That row was stored at park scope because no other EBRPD listing carried the sentence, which is still true -- but Briones' 2026/6 brochure requires five business days for its group camps, and that thread was closed at three on weight of agreement with the five unexplained. Two parks now publish a longer deadline than the District. Not enough to move the row, and enough that the argument for keeping it where it is should be restated honestly rather than left as written.

MAUD WHALEN'S MINIMUM IS 17 ON ITS OWN PAGE AND 25 ON THE PARK'S OVERVIEW, WHICH MAKES THIS THREAD NO LONGER ABOUT ARROYO FLATS. The same split, at a second 75-capacity site, in the same direction: the per-site booking page says 17, the summary page says 25, and the maximum is agreed. Two instances is a pattern in how EBRPD publishes, not a typo at one camp. The conflict_id stays arroyo-flats-minimum because renaming it would orphan the thread's history; the name is now wrong and this entry is where that is recorded. IT ALSO REVERSES THE EVIDENCE UNDER A CORRECTION THIS PROJECT MADE YESTERDAY. Entry -08 corrected the District's capacity tier table -- reconstructed from a flattened PDF -- from 75-to-17 to 75-to-25, on the strength of Maud Whalen being 25 at 75 capacity. That 25 came from the overview page. Maud Whalen's own page says 17, which is what the ORIGINAL reconstruction said. So the reading that was called wrong yesterday now has two per-site pages behind it, and the reading that replaced it has two summary pages. Neither is settled and neither is being restored: the honest state is that the 75 row of that table has two candidate values and no decisive source. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THE OPPOSITE OF ALARMING, AND WORTH STATING PLAINLY: nothing in this dataset derives a figure from that table any more. Its disputed row governed exactly two sites, Maud Whalen and Arroyo Flats, and both now state a number on their own pages. No Anthony Chabot camp is 75 capacity -- their capacities are 300, 100, 100, 50, 50, 35 and 35 -- so the four tiers those rows used are each corroborated by a directly stated site and none of them is the contested one. The table has nothing left to decide and should not be used to derive anything again. FOR A PARTY: 17 to 24 people at either site is the band that turns on this, and group sites book by phone, so the figure a Reservations agent applies decides it. Call.

SEVEN ANTHONY CHABOT GROUP CAMPS CORRECTED FROM DRIVE-IN TO HIKE-IN, ON EVIDENCE THE ROWS WERE ALREADY CARRYING. Every one of them has said 'Vehicles park in the lot nearest the site -- no driving in, and no additional parking passes exist' since the District's group camping sheet was read, while access_mode said drive_in. This project defines drive_in as 'you can park at or beside the site; the car is part of the trip', which is precisely what that sentence denies. THIS IS THE WORST OF THE FOUR ACCESS CORRECTIONS AND IT IS NOT CLOSE. Star Mine, Dairy Glen and Briones each needed a page nobody had read yet. This one needed only reading a row against its own column, and it sat wrong through four days of work that repeatedly discussed exactly this field -- including a commit that said every EBRPD group camp read so far was hike-in while seven rows in the same file said otherwise. IT SURFACED FROM A QUESTION, NOT A SOURCE: asked whether the tool could answer 'which campgrounds near me are drive-in', the filter was run and returned ten rows, seven of which denied it in their own prose. A capability question found a data error, which is an argument for building the query surface rather than against it -- nothing had ever asked this dataset that question before. A GUARD NOW EXISTS, with one exemption that is the point of the two-file split. No drive_in row may contain 'no driving in', 'no driving to site', 'hike-in only' or 'no vehicle access' unless the campground has hike-in rows in campsites.csv. Anthony Chabot Campground earns that exemption: it is a drive-up campground whose Loop B is ten 'Hike-In Sites (NO driving to site)', and the per-site rows carry that. The guard asserts those ten rows exist, so the exemption cannot become a blanket one. DISTANCE IS NOT STATED for any of the seven, unlike the quarter mile at Star Mine, Dairy Glen and Arroyo Flats or Wee-Ta-Chi's 1.5 miles. 'The lot nearest the site' with parking passes issued suggests short; nothing read says so. WHERE THIS LEAVES THE DATASET: three drive-in campgrounds, all family -- Del Valle, Anthony Chabot and Dumbarton Quarry -- and twenty-one reached on foot. Every EBRPD group and backpack camp in this project is now hike-in, with no exceptions and no unsourced values left.

ADDS COORDINATES TO campgrounds.csv AND A SEARCH THAT USES THEM, and the honest headline is that the search can place TWO campgrounds out of twenty-four. Both coordinates already existed in this project as prose, recorded in park_access notes because no table had a field for them: Coyote Hills 37.5575/-122.08583 and Garin 37.62938/-122.02886, each off a ReserveAmerica park overview page. They now sit in columns and reach Dairy Glen and Arroyo Flats. COORD_PRECISION IS THE POINT OF THE SCHEMA, NOT AN ORNAMENT. Every coordinate here names a PARK, because ReserveAmerica publishes a GPS pair on park overview pages and none on campsite pages. A coordinate without that label reads as the campsite's own position, and for a park centroid that can be a mile or more wrong -- the same failure as the guessed access_mode, where a filled field and a checked field rendered identically. The loader REFUSES a coordinate with no precision, refuses half a pair, and refuses a precision with no pair. Blank latitude is None, never 0.0: a zero pair is a real place in the Gulf of Guinea and would sort a campground 8,000 miles away. DUMBARTON QUARRY IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNPLACED although its park now has a coordinate. It resolves to Coyote Hills and has its own entrance several miles round the marsh, and that park resolution is itself 2-2 across sources. Borrowing the centroid would put it somewhere it is not, and a wrong coordinate is worse than none because the search cannot tell. WHAT THE SEARCH REFUSES TO DO. It does not drop what it cannot measure: a campground with no coordinates comes back under CANNOT BE PLACED rather than being omitted, because omitting it makes 'nothing is near you' and 'nobody has looked' identical -- the failure the scorecard already names for Q21. It does not silently swallow the unplaced into a --within bound either; they are unknown, not far. And when --access filters, the campgrounds whose access nobody recorded are listed too, so a list of three cannot read as the whole answer. Today that second list is empty, because as of this morning every campground here has a recorded access mode. THE FEATURE FOUND ITS OWN GAP, WHICH IS THE POINT OF BUILDING IT. Asked for drive-in campgrounds near Oakland, it returns nothing and reports all three as unplaceable. open_questions now asks for the missing coordinates ONE QUESTION PER PARK rather than per campground -- 8 questions, not 22 -- for exactly the reason the campsite-proximity question fires only at hike-in campgrounds: asking it twenty-two times would bury the rest of the list, and the twenty-two share eight answers, one ReserveAmerica overview page each. NOT DONE, AND DELIBERATELY: no coordinate was derived from anything. trailheads.csv has 88 verified pairs and two of them sit in parks that have campgrounds, but a trailhead is not a campground and a derived value dressed as data is the thing this whole schema is built against. No web-search coordinate was taken either. The three drive-in campgrounds need three pages read.

THE COORDINATES THE SEARCH ASKED FOR, AND THE SEARCH NOW ANSWERS ITS OWN QUESTION. Anthony Chabot 37.73528/-122.09611, Del Valle 37.56917/-121.68722, Dumbarton Quarry 37.53109/-122.07305. Drive-in campgrounds from Oakland City Hall now rank: Chabot 10.7 miles, Dumbarton 21.8, Del Valle 35.8, straight-line. Yesterday that query returned nothing and three unplaceable rows. DUMBARTON'S IS THE FIRST CAMPGROUND-PRECISION COORDINATE HERE, because it came off its own ReserveAmerica facility page rather than a park's -- the page's subject IS the campground. AND IT SETTLES WHAT REFUSING TO BORROW COST: the point is about two miles from Coyote Hills' own, so yesterday's decision to leave it blank rather than inherit its park's centroid was worth two miles, in the direction of the marsh. A test now pins that gap. CHABOT'S POINT IS GIVEN TO ALL EIGHT of its campgrounds and DEL VALLE'S TO ONE OF FIVE, and the asymmetry is the rule this schema needed: a park coordinate is assigned when the park's point is a reasonable stand-in for where you arrive, and withheld when a source states a distance that makes it misleading or when the campground has its own entrance. Del Valle's four backpack camps sit 2.07, 6.58, 10.72 and 11.5 miles up the Ohlone Wilderness Trail, measured in this dataset since it began, so the park's point would misplace them by that much. They stay blank and their coord_source says DELIBERATELY UNPLACED and why -- a blank that is a decision has to read as one, which is the same rule as an unsourced access_mode. DEL VALLE ALSO FILLS IN: 7000 Del Valle Rd, Livermore; park phone 510-544-3139; and about nine miles of back road after the I-580 exit, which matters against a gate that shuts at nine or ten. AND IT OPENS A GAP THAT IS NOT A CONFLICT: ReserveAmerica says 'Group campsite gate hours change seasonally' at Del Valle. This project holds NO group campsite at Del Valle -- only the family campground and four backpack camps. Either EBRPD has group sites here that have never been listed, or that sentence is boilerplate. Del Valle is the oldest EBRPD park in this dataset, added 2026-09-04 before any of the per-park reading started, and it is the one park whose campground list has never been checked against a ReserveAmerica campsite page.

DEL VALLE'S GATE CLOSES AT NINE OR AT TEN. The park page, read 2026-09-04, says 6am-9pm May through Labor Day. ReserveAmerica's Del Valle page says 'Park entrance and campground gates close daily at 10 pm', and EBRPD's own District-wide booking alert says campground gates close at 10pm daily -- so two surfaces say ten and one says nine, and the nine is the oldest reading in this dataset. NINE IS KEPT AS THE STORED ANSWER, AGAINST THE WEIGHT AND AGAINST RECENCY, for the reason Anthony Chabot's season is kept closed: the costly direction is arriving at 9:30 on the strength of a ten and finding it shut, nine miles of back road from the freeway, with a car full of camping kit. Being an hour early costs nothing. A READING THAT WOULD RECONCILE THEM AND IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE: the park page's 9pm may be the SEASONAL band it is labelled with, May through Labor Day, while the 10pm is the year-round campground gate -- Anthony Chabot's row already holds exactly that shape, a 10pm campground gate inside 5am-10pm park hours. If so both are right and neither page says which it is describing. Resolving it needs the current Del Valle park page or Reservations on (888) 327-2757 option 3 extension for the park.

DUMBARTON HAS ITS OWN RESERVEAMERICA FACILITY, EB/110750, separate from Coyote Hills' EB/110453 -- more evidence against the park resolution made two days ago, and the third source to arrive since. The tally on whether Dumbarton Quarry Campground sits inside Coyote Hills Regional Park now reads roughly three to one AGAINST: EBRPD's park finder lists it as a park, ReserveAmerica's Coyote Hills page calls it 'a park located nearby', and ReserveAmerica sells it as its own facility -- against the Coyote Hills map brochure listing it under that park's Camping heading. Note that ReserveAmerica is now on both sides of its own evidence. THE RESOLUTION IS KEPT, and the reason is worth arguing with rather than asserting: the brochure's Camping heading is the only one of the four making a claim about BOUNDARIES. A separate booking facility and a park-finder entry are claims about how EBRPD organises its own systems, and Star Mine has a separate entrance at Fredrickson Lane while nobody doubts it lies in Black Diamond. Weight of sources is not the same as weight of relevant sources. ONE CONSEQUENCE HAS GONE AWAY ENTIRELY: this campground now carries its own coordinate, at campground precision, off its own page, so no proximity search depends on the park field to place it. What still depends on it is the $5 parking and the six seasonal gate bands inherited from Coyote Hills, at a camp with its own entrance at 9400 Quarry Road two miles away. That is the live risk, and it is one page from being settled: Dumbarton's own ebparks.org page has never been read here.

Dry Creek Pioneer's park page and the Garin/Dry Creek Pioneer map brochure. ADDS A PARK WITH NO CAMPGROUND, AND THE REFERENTIAL-INTEGRITY GUARD CAUGHT IT IMMEDIATELY -- park_access.park must resolve to a campground or a trailhead, and this park has neither. The guard already had an allowlist for the case, PARKS_WITH_NO_SITE_YET, and putting Dry Creek Pioneer in it would have been a lie: 'nobody has checked' and 'checked, and there is nothing' are the two states this project spends its whole time separating. A second set, PARKS_HELD_WITHOUT_A_SITE, now says which one this is. A DUPLICATE ADVISORY WAS WRITTEN AND DELETED. The Dry Creek Garden closure was filed against Garin yesterday; the garden is actually in Dry Creek Pioneer -- 550 May Road is that park's address, the garden is at the end of May Road, and the shared map puts MEYERS DRY CREEK GARDEN in the Dry Creek Pioneer half. A second row scoped to the right park would have been unreachable, because nothing in this dataset sits in that park, so no plan could ever show it. It stays scoped to Garin, where EBRPD posts it and where a reader planning Arroyo Flats will meet it, with the mis-scoping recorded in the row. What would fix it properly is a unit that can name a paired parkland: two parks, one map, one phone extension, one combined acreage. THE GATE GAP IS NOT A TYPO ON ONE PAGE. Dry Creek Pioneer publishes the same six bands as Garin, band for band, and October 30 and 31 fall in no band here either. EBRPD publishes the same incomplete schedule for both halves of this parkland. A third time band turns up too: the Dry Creek Garden lot is 'open all week until dusk', which is neither the gate nor the 10pm curfew. AN ASYMMETRY RECORDED WITHOUT BEING OVER-READ: Garin's page says 'Garin only accepts cash for payment' and this near-identical page says nothing about payment at all. An absent sentence is not a statement that cards are taken. THE PICNIC LEAD TIME CONTRADICTS ITSELF IN TWO PARAGRAPHS OF ONE PAGE -- 'up to 3 working days prior' and 'at least 14 days in advance', about the same four areas. No conflict thread, because nothing here books a picnic area, but it is the third EBRPD lead-time disagreement found in three days, after Briones' five-business-days brochure and Coyote Hills' five working days, and the first where one page disagrees with itself. NOT CAPTURED: the four reservable group picnic areas are not campgrounds and get no rows, the same call made for Briones' Oak Grove, Newt Hollow and Crow. The Meyers sisters' history, the iris garden's spring season and the planned cottage visitor centre went into prose.

TWO OF THE THREE CANDIDATE EXPLANATIONS FOR THE 15-VERSUS-18 PARK COUNT TURN OUT TO BE THE SAME PARK. That is the finding, and it makes the reconciliation sharper and the remaining gap clearer. The three readings offered when this opened were: the finder tagging a park whose camping Reservations does not handle; Dumbarton Quarry counted separately while sitting inside Coyote Hills; and Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer being one parkland with two entries. DRY CREEK PIONEER IS BOTH THE FIRST AND THE THIRD. Its park page carries the Camping activity icon. There is no ReserveAmerica facility for it. The single brochure covering both parks has one 'Reservable Camp' symbol in its legend and uses it once, for ARROYO FLATS GROUP CAMP, keyed to the Garin Avenue Staging Area inset in the Garin half. So it is a park the finder tags for camping whose camping Reservations does not handle, AND it is half of the paired parkland -- one over-count, not two. THE ARITHMETIC NOW WORKS, AND ARITHMETIC THAT WORKS IS NOT EVIDENCE. That lesson is already in this log, from the Anthony Chabot site count where clean arithmetic produced a confident wrong correction. Eighteen minus Dumbarton, minus Dry Creek Pioneer, minus Tilden Nature Area is fifteen. Two of those three subtractions now rest on read sources; THE TILDEN ONE RESTS ON NOTHING. The finder list contains both Charles Lee Tilden Regional Park and Tilden Nature Area, and whether that is one park or two has never been checked here. The sum landing on fifteen is a reason to go and read Tilden's pages, not a substitute for reading them. AND THE DUMBARTON SUBTRACTION IS ITSELF CONTESTED, three sources to one against this project's own resolution as of this morning. So the honest state is: one over-count evidenced and solid (Dry Creek Pioneer), one evidenced and disputed (Dumbarton), one guessed to make the sum work (Tilden). The thread stays open. What closes it is Tilden's park pages and Dumbarton's own ebparks.org page, neither of which has been read.

Reinhardt Redwood's park page and its map brochure. ADDS THE ONLY PARK IN THIS PROJECT WITH AN OAKLAND ADDRESS -- 7867 Redwood Road, 'a few miles over the ridge from downtown Oakland' -- three park-scoped facts, two new regulations and three advisories, one of them the first danger-rated row in that table. ADDS ONE CAMP WHERE THE PAGE CLAIMS SEVERAL, AND LEAVES THE REST AS A GAP. 'Several group overnight camping areas are located throughout the park.' The map's legend distinguishes Reservable Group Camp from Reservable Picnic Area and the only label containing the word camp is GIRLS' CAMP, marked 'Closed in winter'. Other named places on the sheet -- Trail's End, Big Bend Meadow, Orchard, Old Church, Fern Dell, Anna Costa, Quail, Owl -- carry one symbol or the other and the PDF flattens to text, so the symbols do not survive. Three of them are the three reservable picnic sites the page counts. NAMING A CAMP FROM THAT LIST WOULD BE THE BRIONES ERROR, where a map labelled Oak Grove, Newt Hollow and Crow the same way as three group camps and half of them were picnic areas. One camp recorded, 'several' left open. ACCESS MODE IS BLANK ON PURPOSE, and ACCESS_MODE_UNRECORDED stops being empty for the first time since Briones left it. Four access corrections in four days, three of them because a value was written that no page supported; nothing is written here. The lesson applied on the way in instead of a day later. THE NARROWEST FEE IN THIS PROJECT AND THE FIRST CHARGED AT ONE ENTRANCE RATHER THAN AT A PARK: weekends and major holidays, April through October, when staffed, AND ONLY AT REDWOOD GATE. About a dozen other entrances take no money. Every park_access row here treats a fee as a property of the park, which is wrong for this one -- there is no per-entrance fee field, and that is a schema limit rather than a data gap. Cash only, the third such park after Garin and Briones. FIVE GATE BANDS THAT COVER THE WHOLE YEAR, which settles something about Garin. Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer both leave October 30 and 31 in no band; this park's months abut cleanly, so that two-day hole is a defect on those two pages rather than a District style. THREE ADVISORIES. Stream Trail closed for repairs from Trail's End through Fern Trail since Aug 24 -- THE FIRST ROW IN THIS TABLE TO CARRY A START DATE, a field that has never been used because everything else was already in force when read. A second Stream Trail shutdown at Old Church picnic site in 'late September and early October', stored with NO DATES because that phrase is not a date and writing one would be inventing precision, the same error as a guessed coordinate. And A BOIL WATER ADVISORY on the system serving Piedmont Stables -- the first danger-rated advisory here and the first water fact that is not about availability. Every water row this project holds answers 'is the spigot running'; this one says it is running and must not be drunk untreated. IT COULD NOT GO IN water_sources: that table's location must resolve to a trailhead or a campground name and Piedmont Stables is a staging area, so the fact reaches a reader through the park instead. The linked Boil Water Notice PDF has not been read, so the cause, the start date and what was detected are all unknown. TWO PARK-SCOPED RULES. The Redwood Creek Resource Protection Area requires dogs on leash on Stream and Bridle Trails and keeps PEOPLE as well as dogs out of the creek and off its banks -- the only rule here that restricts humans for habitat, filed under pets because this vocabulary has no habitat category. And FISHING IS NOT ALLOWED anywhere in the park, the first fishing rule in the dataset, and notable because Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer both advertise fishing. NOT CAPTURED: the three reservable picnic sites for 50-75, which are not camps, the same call made for Briones' Oak Grove and Garin's four areas; the archery range, Redwood Bowl, the Anna Costa amphitheatre and the Fishway Interpretive Site went into park notes. EBRPD links an Access Northern California accessibility page and states it has not reviewed it and does not guarantee its accuracy, which is carried as published -- an agency declining to vouch for its own link is worth a reader's attention.

Reinhardt Redwood's four ReserveAmerica pages. ANSWERS 'SEVERAL' WITH A NUMBER: three group camps -- Fern Dell (17-50), Girl's Camp (17-50) and Trail's End (17-25). Yesterday the park page claimed several and the map named one, and this project recorded one camp and left the rest as a stated gap rather than guessing from eight labels. TWO OF THE EIGHT WERE CAMPS. Naming them from that list would have been wrong five times out of eight, which is what the Briones lesson was worth here. GIRLS' CAMP'S BLANK ACCESS MODE IS FILLED FROM A SOURCE, one commit after it was left blank. That is the whole argument for blanks: it was never a guess, so nothing had to be corrected. All three sites read Site Access: Hike-In, and the page says why in a sentence no other EBRPD park has put so plainly -- 'Driving into the sites is not permitted. BRING WAGONS to transport items to/from.' A CORRECTION TO A BRIONES NOTE, AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN MISREADING. The Briones rows say 'the booking system shows Briones open through 31 October 2026' as one of the surfaces confirming a 1 November closure. This page shows 'Current Status - Open Through 06 Jan 2027' and then states 'All group campsites are closed seasonally, November 1 - May 15' -- nine weeks apart. So the Open Through field is a booking-horizon or facility-status date, NOT a season end. At Briones the two happened to coincide and the coincidence was read as corroboration. The Briones closure still stands on three independent surfaces; it is the count of surfaces that was wrong, and the same misreading would have mattered somewhere it did not coincide. TRAIL'S END HAS THE TIGHTEST PARTY BAND HERE: 17 to 25, eight people wide, at a park fifteen minutes from downtown Oakland. It is also the camp the Stream Trail repair closure names directly -- 'beginning Mon., Aug. 24, 2026 FROM TRAIL'S END through Fern Trail' -- and Fern Dell sits on the same stretch. Whether those closures block the walk in from the Wayside Overflow lot is stated nowhere, and that is now a specific question for Reservations rather than the open-ended unknown it was yesterday. '3 DAYS' FINALLY HAS A DEFINITION. The booking rules say 'at least 72 hours (3 days) prior', the first time any surface gives this deadline in hours. So the booking system's floor is calendar hours and EBRPD's prose floor is three BUSINESS days: a Friday call for a Monday arrival clears one and fails the other. Carried into the group booking channel. THE GROUP CANCELLATION SCHEDULE, which this project has never had: 14+ days 90% of site fees refundable, 13-3 days 50%, under 3 days nothing. Changes impossible under 3 days and $8 above it. Damage deposit one night's fee, fully refundable, but repaid in 14-21 days by card and 4-6 WEEKS by cheque. TWO NEW RULES AND TWO REFINEMENTS. A District prohibited list -- no drones, no balloons or pinatas, nothing hung from trees, no feeding or approaching wildlife, NO RELEASING ANIMALS INTO PARKLANDS, no damaging plants or geological or archaeological features, no wading or swimming in undesignated areas. A park stay limit of 7 nights a month and 30 a year, filed at park scope because only this page states a number and this table has no scope for a class of site; Garin's copy of the same block says only that stay limits 'vary by site type', which is what this looks like the answer to. THE PROVENANCE GUARD FLAGGED IT IMMEDIATELY and correctly -- the number exists on the booking platform and nowhere on ebparks.org. THE FISHING RULE IS REFINED AND COMPLICATED: the park page bans fishing anywhere in the park, this page bans 'Fishing in Redwood Creek, either in the park OR ALONG REDWOOD ROAD'. A park rule that follows a creek outside its own boundary, which nothing else here does. No conflict thread -- they overlap rather than contradict, and nothing anywhere says fishing is permitted. AND THE DOG CONFINEMENT CLAUSE TRACKS THE ACCESS MODE, which is a small thing worth seeing: Garin says a dog must be confined to a VEHICLE OR TENT during quiet hours, Reinhardt says a TENT. Reinhardt's camps ban driving in, so there is no vehicle at the site. NO CELL SERVICE, WIFI OR INTERNET ANYWHERE IN THIS PARK, stated in capitals, with a PAYPHONE near the main entrance on Redwood Road and EBRPD Dispatch on 510-881-1121 emergency and 510-881-1833 non-emergency. Fifty people can be a quarter-hour from downtown Oakland with no way to call out from the site. THE SPELLING IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS TWO SOURCES AND WITHIN ONE: the map prints GIRLS' CAMP, the site list prints "Girl's Camp", and the same page's Vehicles paragraph prints 'Girls Camp'. The map spelling is kept as the row name; the others are recorded because searching the booking site for the wrong one finds nothing.

Las Trampas' park page, its map and its four ReserveAmerica pages. BREAKS THE RULE THIS PROJECT WAS ABOUT TO BELIEVE: Corral Camp states 'Site Access: Drive-In'. Sixteen group camps here were hike-in, three of them corrected FROM a wrong drive_in over the last four days, and that was hardening into a District fact. It was a fact about the eight parks read first. The page even adds a field nothing else has used, 'Driveway Entry: Pull-Through'. IT IS THE SECOND-CLOSEST CAMPING TO OAKLAND IN THIS DATASET at 11.7 straight-line miles, behind Anthony Chabot's 10.7, and the only drive-in one of the two that is a group camp. It is also an EQUESTRIAN camp -- 'Pets Allowed: Domestic, Horse', category 'Group Site, Horse Site' -- the second after Stewartville. Minimum 17, maximum 50, 10 vehicles, five 6ft tables, a serving table, two XL BBQs, two chemical toilets, and EBRPD's own sentence 'COWS AND COW PIES MAY BE PRESENT'. A THIRD SEASONAL PATTERN: closed 1 November - 31 MARCH, where Briones and Reinhardt Redwood are both 1 November - 15 May. Five months against five and a half, reopening six weeks earlier. The 'Open Through 31 Oct 2026' field agrees with the season here, having disagreed with it by nine weeks at Reinhardt yesterday -- which is the point of yesterday's correction: it coincides sometimes and is not evidence either way. THE GATE BANDS OVERLAP WHERE GARIN'S LEAVE A HOLE. March 8 is the end of one band and the start of the next, closing at 6pm by one line and 7pm by the other. Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer leave October 30 and 31 in no band at all. Two defects in the same field, on the same kind of page, in opposite directions -- EBRPD's seasonal bands are typed by hand and nothing checks them for coverage. 6pm is stored as the one that does not strand anybody. 5:30pm is the first non-hour closing time in this project, and NO CURFEW is published here where four other parks state 10pm-5am. NO PARKING FEE IS PUBLISHED AT ALL -- not a stated 'no fee' like Anthony Chabot's, but no Fees section on the page. Recorded as silence rather than as free, which is the same rule the campground fee field follows. WATER IS THE FIRST SOURCE IN THIS PROJECT THE OPERATOR CALLS UNRELIABLE RATHER THAN MERELY UNCHECKED. Two faucets with spigots exist; the booking system, the park page and the map all say the supply is inconsistent and may be unavailable at any time, and EBRPD asks campers to phone park staff before a reservation. Recorded as one water_sources row -- not two, because nothing distinguishes the faucets -- with a log entry whose status is 'not guaranteed' and whose note says plainly that nobody has turned these taps. THE LEDGER'S USUAL LOGIC DOES NOT APPLY HERE: a newer check normally supersedes an older one, and no check can supersede 'may run out at any time'. Potable is left BLANK rather than False -- the map legend marks Drinking Water and EBRPD never uses the word. THE EBMUD PERMIT REACHES A THIRD PARK. The map marks the adjoining San Leandro Watershed 'Hiking permit required: call (510) 287-0459', a number this project did not have. After the Chabot-to-Garin trail and the Briones Reservoir land, that permit is a boundary condition of the whole District rather than a feature of one park. The map also shows the EUGENE O'NEILL NATIONAL HISTORIC SITE adjoining -- National Park Service, a fifth agency touching these parks. ACREAGE DISAGREES 6,050 AGAINST 5,342 and gets no thread, the same call as Coyote Hills' 1,266 against 978. THE PARK'S NAME DISAGREES TOO: ebparks.org says Las Trampas Wilderness Regional Preserve, its own booking system says Las Trampas Regional Wilderness. NOT CAPTURED: Steelhead and Shady picnic areas, and the Little Hills Picnic Ranch, which takes group picnics of 50 to 1,000 through a CONCESSIONAIRE number, (925) 837-8158, rather than EBRPD Reservations. Recorded in park notes only, with the observation that the District's 'a reservation obtained from anyone but EBRPD is void' rule is about campsites and does not collide with it -- written down so nobody has to work that out twice. The geology, the plant list and the etymology of Las Trampas went nowhere. ONE LOADER BUG THE WATER ROW EXPOSED, AND IT WAS THE WORST FIELD TO HAVE IT IN. water_sources.potable was a plain bool defaulting to False, so a blank cell loaded as 'not potable' -- a claim nobody made, about the one field where being wrong in either direction is a health question. It is now three-valued, None for a blank, the same rule already applied to access_mode, fees and coordinates. NO COMMITTED ROW CHANGED MEANING: every other row in that table states True or False explicitly, and Las Trampas' faucets are the only blank -- EBRPD marks Drinking Water on its map, never uses the word potable, and says the supply may run out at any time. The bug had been latent since the table was built because nothing had ever been genuinely unknown before.

CORRAL CAMP HAS TWO XL BARBECUES AND A RULE THAT SAYS NO BARBECUES, ON THE SAME LISTING. ReserveAmerica's description of the site: 'It has five 6' tables, a serving table, TWO XL BBQs, and two chemical toilets.' The site details flag 'BBQ: Y'. The campground rules block on the same pages: 'No campfires/BBQ's. Camp stoves ok.' The park's own Facilities paragraph says 'NO campfires are permitted' and says nothing about barbecues either way. FILED AS INTERNAL BECAUSE ONE PUBLISHER CONTRADICTS ITSELF -- the description, the amenity flag and the rules block are three parts of one ReserveAmerica listing. That matters for how it gets resolved: there is no question of ranking publishers, and no newer-source-wins to apply. THREE READINGS, NONE STATED. The rules block may be District boilerplate pasted onto a park whose camp predates it, in which case the furnished BBQs are usable and the sentence is wrong here. Or the ban is real and the two XL BBQs are decommissioned or reserved for staff, in which case the description and the amenity flag are stale. Or 'BBQ's' in that sentence means PERSONAL portable barbecues, which Ordinance 38 s.404 permits generally and which a park with a fire ban might single out -- leaving the fixed units usable. Black Diamond is the test case that argues against reading this as a plain total ban: it bans campfires AND barbecues park-wide, and its camps carry NO BBQ flag. There the facilities match the rule. Here they do not. WHY IT IS WORTH A THREAD rather than a caveat: a group of up to fifty planning to cook over the provided barbecues, at a camp where campfires are banned and camp stoves are the stated alternative, will either eat or not depending on which reading is right. The conservative plan is camp stoves for everyone. Resolving it needs Reservations on (888) 327-2757 option 2, or the park on (510) 544-3276.

Mission Peak's park page and map. FILLS THE THINNEST CAMPGROUND ROW LEFT IN THIS PROJECT -- Eagle Springs had a park, an access mode, a restroom flag and one sentence of notes, and it arrived through the Ohlone Wilderness corridor rather than through a camping page. TWO SPELLINGS, BOTH EBRPD'S OWN. The park page and the map say EAGLE SPRING BACKPACK CAMP, singular; the District's Ohlone corridor water update, which is where this row's name came from, says 'Eagle Springs'. The plural is KEPT as the key, deliberately: the water source and its append-only check ledger are built on it, and renaming would leave two ledger entries dangling against a guard that checks exactly that join. Recording both spellings costs nothing; rewriting an append-only ledger to tidy a name costs the thing the ledger is for. 'WATER NEEDS TO BE TREATED OR BOILED', on the map and again on the park page. That is stronger and more useful than the non-potable flag it corroborates: the water is THERE and usable, with a stove and time, rather than simply undrinkable. The potable column cannot express the difference, which is the same column that went three-valued yesterday for Las Trampas. Two parks in two days pressing on one boolean. THE SECOND PER-ENTRANCE FAILURE OF park_access IN TWO DAYS, and that makes it a structural gap rather than an awkward fit. Reinhardt Redwood charges at one entrance of about a dozen; Mission Peak publishes TWO SETS OF HOURS -- Ohlone College daily year-round 6am-10pm, Stanford Avenue 6:30am-8pm or 9pm by season. This row holds one pair. Stanford Avenue's are stored because it is the only entrance where a camper may park overnight, and that choice is written into the row rather than left to be inferred. THE ONLY FEE AT THIS PARK IS CHARGED BY A COMMUNITY COLLEGE. EBRPD charges nothing at either entrance; Ohlone College charges $4 and has required a permit displayed 6am-11pm every day, weekends included, since November 2017. So the trip's cost roll-up now shows a park_entrance component whose money goes to someone who is not the land manager -- and an agent that dropped it because the District is free would under-price the trip. A TEST NOW PINS THAT. AND THE ENTRANCE EBRPD RECOMMENDS IS THE ONE A CAMPER CANNOT USE: overnight parking is banned at Ohlone College. Stanford Avenue is free, has 43 spaces, and needs the overnight permit issued with the camping reservation. A THIRD PARTY CLOSES THE STREETS TOO -- the City of Fremont's residential permit programme restricts non-resident parking from Saturday 12:01am through Sunday 11:59pm and on national holidays, which is exactly when the 43-space lot fills. THE FIRST PUBLISHED PENALTY IN THIS DATASET: 'Visitors found inside the park, entrance area, and parking lot after posted hours will be subject to citation and or arrest. Citations cost a minimum of $300.' WHETHER A RESERVATION EXEMPTS THE CAMPER IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE READ, and a backpacker with a booking is inside the park all night by design. The overnight permit covers the car. Nothing read covers the person. THE HAZARD EBRPD LEADS WITH IS HEAT AND IT IS ADDRESSED TO DOG OWNERS: 'Every year, several dogs die of heat stroke and dehydration at Mission Peak.' Two litres for you and your dog, water the dog every time you drink, cooler temperatures only, watch for heavy panting, dry gums, weakness, inattention. It is a standing fact rather than an advisory with an end, so it went into park notes -- and it is the clearest example yet of what the scorecard's no-model 'What is hazardous right now?' actually costs a reader. A SIXTH AGENCY: San Francisco Water District land adjoins, posted 'STAY ON TRAIL! NO BICYCLES', after EBMUD, the National Park Service, US Fish and Wildlife and the District. Acreage disagrees 3,023 on the page against 3,043 on the map -- twenty acres, no thread, and the smallest such gap yet between two documents from the same publisher, so probably a typo rather than two measurements. Trail mileages worth keeping: 3.59 miles from the Mission Peak boundary to Sunol's, 8.66 miles from Stanford Avenue to the Sunol Visitor Center. A GUARD CAUGHT A DUPLICATION AS IT WAS WRITTEN. The map prints the reservations number beside the camp, and it went into reservation_contact for about a minute before the test that exists to stop exactly that fired: agency-wide booking mechanics live once, in booking_channels.csv. The number stays in prose as the map's own wording and out of the field a renderer would present. NOT CAPTURED: the Scarface restoration, the 2012-13 volunteer work, the feral goats, Kalpana Chawla, and the footwear advice.

MISSION PEAK REFINES THE PARK-COUNT THREAD BY RULING OUT AN INFERENCE THIS PROJECT WAS ONE STEP FROM MAKING. Dry Creek Pioneer is tagged for camping and has no ReserveAmerica facility, and it turned out to have no camp -- which invites the rule 'no booking facility means no camping park, so it is an over-count'. MISSION PEAK BREAKS THAT RULE. It has no ReserveAmerica facility either, and it has a real camp: Eagle Spring Backpack Camp, named on the park page and on the park map, bookable by phone. EBRPD's backpack sites are phone-only across the whole District and were never sold online, so the absence of a facility says nothing about whether a park has camping. WHAT SEPARATES THE TWO CASES IS THE CAMP, NOT THE FACILITY. Dry Creek Pioneer's shared map with Garin shows one Reservable Camp symbol and it is in the Garin half. Mission Peak's map prints EAGLE SPRING BACKPACK CAMP with its rules beside it. So the Dry Creek Pioneer over-count still stands, and it stands on the map rather than on the missing facility. THE THREAD IS UNCHANGED OTHERWISE and the arithmetic still rests on one untested subtraction, Tilden Nature Area. Recorded because an inference that would have been convenient and wrong is worth writing down when a source rules it out.

Morgan Territory's park page and map. ADDS A PARK, A BACKPACK CAMP AND A TRAIL CLOSURE, and the camp arrives with a name nobody published. THE NAME IS CONSTRUCTED AND THE ROW SAYS SO IN ITS FIRST SENTENCE. The park page says only 'There is a backpack campsite in the Regional Preserve'; the map labels it 'BACKPACK CAMP'. Nothing read names it. 'Morgan Territory Backpack Camp' follows the form EBRPD uses on its own alerts page -- 'Round Valley Backpack Camp at Round Valley Regional Preserve' -- and it is a key rather than a claim. THE RISK IS EXACTLY THE ONE THIS PROJECT KEEPS MEETING: a constructed value renders identically to a sourced one, which is how a guessed access_mode survived four days. So it is flagged in the row, and any published name wins over it. SIX GATE BANDS THAT COVER THE YEAR EXACTLY, no hole and no overlap -- the third clean set, with Reinhardt Redwood, against Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer's two missing days and Las Trampas' one doubled day. AND THE PARK HOURS ARE NOT THE GATE HOURS: 'Open 5am-10pm unless otherwise posted OR PERMITTED.' Those last two words are the first evidence in this dataset that EBRPD contemplates a permit extending a park's hours, which bears on the question left open at Mission Peak yesterday -- whether a camping reservation exempts a backpacker from posted hours and a $300 minimum citation. It is not an answer for Mission Peak, whose page says hours are strictly enforced and uses different words. It is the first sign the exemption exists anywhere. 'PARKING: NO FEE', stated. Recorded against Las Trampas, whose page has no Fees section at all and is filed here as silence -- this is what a stated no-fee looks like and the two must not read the same. THE BACKPACK CAMP IS NOT WHEELCHAIR ACCESSIBLE, stated outright. First explicit NOT-accessible statement in this dataset; every other accessibility note here says what IS accessible and leaves the rest to inference. TWO MORE AGENCIES, TAKING THE COUNT TO EIGHT. Mount Diablo State Park adjoins to the west. The LOS VAQUEROS WATERSHED, run by the Contra Costa Water District, adjoins to the east and EBRPD prints its conditions on its own map: 'On-Trail Use Only. NO DOGS ALLOWED', with 1.64 miles through it from Round Valley to the Manzanita Trail here, ccwater.com/412, (925) 240-2360. So the walk between two parks this project holds crosses a third party's land that bans dogs, and neither park's own dog rules would tell you. Same shape as the EBMUD trail permit, which now touches three parks. FIRST PARKING CAPACITY AND FIRST STAGING-AREA ELEVATION for an EBRPD park: 95 spots at 2,030 feet, both off the map. STONE CORRAL TRAIL IS CLOSED between Coyote Trail and the Highland Ridge junction for storm damage, the fifth storm closure in the advisories table. IT NAMES THE TRAIL THE CAMP SITS BESIDE: the map puts the camp on Roger Epperson Ridge between the Clyma and Highland Ridge Trails. Whether the closure blocks a route to it is not stated and cannot be told from a flattened map -- the same open question as Reinhardt Redwood, where a Stream Trail closure names Trail's End and Fern Dell. Two parks now. NOT CAPTURED: the wildflowers, the Diablo sunflower, the helmet law EBRPD prints for cyclists under 18, and the private-property gates went into park notes rather than becoming rows.

IS ROUND VALLEY'S CAMP A BACKPACK CAMP OR A GROUP CAMP? Two EBRPD sources say different things, and the answer changes which queue you book it in. This project stores it as BACKPACK, from the District's own alerts page -- 'Round Valley Backpack Camp at Round Valley Regional Preserve is not working' -- and its ReserveAmerica booking page. MORGAN TERRITORY'S MAP, which shows the adjoining preserve, labels the same camp 'ROUND VALLEY GROUP CAMP'. IT IS NOT A NAMING QUIBBLE, WHICH IS WHY IT GETS A THREAD. campsite_type keys into booking_channels.csv, and EBRPD's two classes have different mechanics: backpack sites are phone-only at 48 hours' notice, group sites are phone-only at 72 hours (3 days) with a tiered cancellation schedule and a damage deposit of one night's fee. A party booking on the wrong class's deadline calls too late. BACKPACK IS KEPT, on two grounds. The alerts page and the booking page are both about THIS camp, where the map is about a neighbouring park and labels its surroundings; and the camp's own recorded capacity is minimum 1, maximum 25, which is a backpack shape -- every group camp in this dataset has a minimum of 17 or more, and a site a solo camper can book is not a group site. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is the heading Round Valley's own ReserveAmerica campsites page files it under; that page was read for capacity and facilities and the heading was not recorded, which is this project's omission rather than a gap in the source.

Morgan Territory's three ReserveAmerica pages, one day after the camp was added from a park page and a map. THE CONSTRUCTED NAME TURNED OUT TO BE THE PUBLISHED ONE: the row was keyed 'Morgan Territory Backpack Camp' because nothing read named the camp, and the booking system calls it exactly that. A convention holding is not a licence to construct names -- the flag was right to be there and would have been right if the name had been wrong. It stays in the row. PARKING IS APPROXIMATELY 4.5 MILES FROM THE SITE, the longest carry in this project by more than a mile: Stewartville 3.2, Wee-Ta-Chi 1.5, and a quarter mile at Star Mine, Dairy Glen and Arroyo Flats. The park's coordinate is park precision and is therefore nowhere near this camp, which the coord_source now says. Minimum 1, maximum 20. THE SENTENCE THIS PROJECT HAS BEEN MISSING: 'Campers are restricted to campsite during curfew hours (10pm-5am).' That answers the question left open at Mission Peak two entries ago -- a reservation DOES let you be in the park overnight, and what it costs is the freedom to move. Mission Peak warns of citation or arrest after posted hours with a $300 minimum and says nothing about campers; this park's own hours read 'unless otherwise posted or permitted'. Three sentences from three pages, none of them about Mission Peak's camp, and together they are the clearest answer available. AND MOST OF THE ROUND VALLEY CLASS PUZZLE DISSOLVES. This camp's page heading is BACKPACK SITE, its loop is 'Backpack Seasonal', its minimum is 1 -- and its 'Looking For Category' reads 'Group Site, Horse Site, Tent Site'. So that field is a MULTI-VALUED SEARCH FACET, not a class. A camp can be tagged group and be a backpack site, which is most of why a neighbouring park's map could label Round Valley's camp a group camp. The thread stays open, because the map is still a separate source and the facet finding explains rather than settles it, but the reading has firmed up considerably. FACILITIES: picnic tables, a vault toilet, hitching rails, a horse trough and NON-POTABLE water -- filter, treat, boil or bring your own, which at 4.5 miles means carrying every litre that far. has_restroom corrected from blank to True, restroom_type to vault toilet. Pets Allowed: Domestic, Horse, the third equestrian camp here. 'DO NOT CAMP UNDER THE TREES, USE OPEN SPACE' -- no other camp in this dataset says where within the site to pitch. SEASON IS 1 NOVEMBER - 1 APRIL, a fourth shape in this District after Briones and Reinhardt Redwood at 15 May and Las Trampas at 31 March. TWO NUMBERS ADDED TO THE BOOKING CHANNELS. A special event permit for a publicly advertised event must be on file AT LEAST 60 DAYS ahead -- every other surface says only that the permit is needed, and 60 days is longer than the window in which a backpack site can be booked at all. And the information letter carrying the parking passes arrives 'approximately one week' before, which is a THIRD figure for the same letter after 5-7 days on the group row and 5-10 on Arroyo Flats' own page. CITY AND COUNTY ARE PUBLISHED TWO WAYS: the park page says Livermore, CA 94551, which is Alameda County; ReserveAmerica says Eastern Contra Costa County, city of Antioch, with no ZIP. Both EBRPD's, identical directions, and nothing here turns on it, so no thread. NOT CAPTURED beyond prose: the Volvon homeland statement, the emergency numbers and EBRPD's own warning that cell reception may be spotty inside parks -- which matters at a camp 4.5 miles from the road with one 911-only telephone on the map.

HOW MANY VEHICLES MAY A PARTY BRING TO MORGAN TERRITORY'S BACKPACK CAMP? The site details say 'Maximum Number of Vehicles: 4'. The same page's own notes say 'PARKING: 5 parking passes; NO overflow parking.' One page, two numbers, four against five. INTERNAL, AND THE SECOND INSTANCE OF EXACTLY THIS DEFECT. Stewartville's listing says maximum 1 vehicle in its structured detail and 5 parking passes in its notes, and that thread has been open since Black Diamond was read. Two sites now where the structured field and the prose disagree about the same quantity, which suggests the two are maintained separately rather than one being a typo. Everywhere the two AGREE -- Wee-Ta-Chi 10 and 10, Arroyo Flats 15 and 15 -- passes and vehicles are the same number, so a pass is a vehicle and the fields are measuring the same thing. THE STAKE IS SMALLER THAN STEWARTVILLE'S and it is not nothing: with no overflow parking and roadside parking 'highly discouraged', a fifth car that turns up on the strength of a fifth pass has nowhere legal to go. Plan on four. Resolving it needs Reservations on (888) 327-2757 option 2, and the same call would settle Stewartville.

THE OHLONE WILDERNESS PERMIT WAS ABOLISHED ON 1 JANUARY 2026, AND EBRPD STILL PUBLISHES TWO MAPS THAT REQUIRE IT. Sunol's park page: 'As of 1/1/2026, an Ohlone permit will NOT be required and no additional permits will be sold. No refunds for permits purchased in 2025. Backpacking reservations are still required if you plan on staying overnight.' NOTHING IN THIS DATASET CHANGES, AND THAT IS THE POINT WORTH RECORDING. Both Ohlone trailheads have carried permit_group 'none' since they were added. A blank that was never filled and a sourced absence with a date look identical in a column and are not the same claim -- the same distinction this project has now drawn for access_mode, for potable, for fees and for coordinates. This one is now sourced. THE STALE-SOURCE TRAP IS LIVE. The Sunol park map says 'OHLONE WILDERNESS TRAIL PERMIT IS REQUIRED FOR EACH PERSON to hike beyond Sunol Regional Park boundary into Ohlone Regional Wilderness', tells you where to buy one, and repeats 'Ohlone Trail Permit required' beside the boundary. The second PDF is linked off the same park page under the filename Ohlone-Wilderness-Permit-Map-11x17.pdf and explains what the permit covers -- 'foot and equestrian use of the trail only'. Both are current links from a page that abolishes the thing they describe. A planner reading either map alone would try to buy a permit that is no longer sold. Recorded on both Ohlone trailheads and on Sunol Backpack Camp, where a reader will meet it. WHAT SURVIVES: backpacking reservations, 2 or more business days ahead by phone, and the overnight PARKING permit issued with a camping reservation at Stanford Avenue. Neither is the Ohlone permit, and Sunol's map adds a third that is nothing to do with it -- 'Membership or Permit required to park on Welch Creek Road', obtained at the Sunol entry kiosk, the only per-road parking permit in this project. ADDS SUNOL'S PARK ACCESS ROW: six gate bands covering the year exactly, the fourth clean set; $5 weekends and holidays; cash, Visa, MasterCard, Discover and tap to pay. THERE IS NO DRINKING WATER IN THE PARK, stated twice on the park page -- and the spring-fed spigot this project holds at Sunol Backpack Camp is non-potable, so both are true at once. This is the only park whose own page says the second half outright. PUBLIC WIFI AT THE VISITOR CENTER, the first in this project, against Reinhardt Redwood's 'NO CELL SERVICE, WIFI/INTERNET AT THIS PARK'. THE PERMIT MAP CONFIRMS SUNOL'S SEVEN SITE NAMES and disagrees with one spelling: it numbers them 1-Cathedral, 2-Oak View, 3-Sycamore, 4-Stars Rest, 5-Hawks Nest, 6-EAGLES EYRIE, 7-Sky Camp, where this project has 'Eagles Aerie'. Same word, two spellings, third EBRPD naming disagreement in three days after Eagle Spring(s) and Girls'/Girl's Camp. Key kept, map spelling recorded. MILEAGES THAT TIE THREE PARKS TOGETHER: 8.66 miles Sunol Visitor Center to Stanford Avenue at Mission Peak, 13.9 miles Sunol boundary to Del Valle boundary, 15.6 to Del Valle West Beach. Visitor Center 390 feet, Sunol Backpack Camp 1,699.

CLOSES A GAP OPENED TWO DAYS AGO: DEL VALLE HAS FIVE MORE CAMPS. When Del Valle's ReserveAmerica page said 'Group campsite gate hours change seasonally', this project held no group campsite at Del Valle at all and logged it as a gap with the note that Del Valle is the oldest EBRPD park here and the one whose campground list has never been checked. The Ohlone Wilderness permit map names them: WILD TURKEY GROUP CAMP, PUNTA VACA GROUP CAMP, CEDAR GROUP CAMP, LIL CHAPARRAL HORSE CAMP and CABALLO LOCO HORSE CAMP, clustered by the Del Valle Family Campground. WHY THESE ARE ADDED WHERE REINHARDT REDWOOD'S EIGHT LABELS WERE NOT. There the map distinguished Reservable Group Camp from Reservable Picnic Area by SYMBOL, the flattened PDF lost the symbols, and guessing from the labels would have been wrong five times in eight. Here the type is in the name, in words. That is the difference between reading a map and guessing at one. ADDS A CAMPSITE CLASS: EQUESTRIAN, for the two horse camps. It is EBRPD's own word, from the cancellation text attached to every reservation -- 'to change/cancel a backpacking, equestrian, or group camping reservation' -- not a class invented here to hold rows that did not fit. booking_channels has no equestrian row, so resolving one of these returns the District-wide contact and NO class-specific method, which is the honest answer: nobody here knows how an equestrian site is booked. EVERYTHING ELSE ABOUT ALL FIVE IS BLANK and the rows say so: no capacity, no minimum, no fee, no water, no restroom, no season, and ACCESS MODE NOT RECORDED. ACCESS_MODE_UNRECORDED stops being empty again -- it has now emptied and refilled three times, which is the argument for keeping the set rather than deleting it when it happens to be empty. THE COST ROLL-UP FELT IT IMMEDIATELY. A Rose Peak plan now carries SIX unpriced campground components where it carried one, every one of them saying NO FEE ON FILE rather than vanishing. That is the intended behaviour and it is also a fair warning: this park's data is thinner than it looks, and one ReserveAmerica campsites page would fill all five rows at once.

ONE RESERVEAMERICA FACILITY SELLS NINETEEN BACKPACK SITES ACROSS THREE PARKS, and finding it explains two absences this project had already recorded without understanding. EB/110028 is titled simply 'Sunol' -- not Sunol Regional Wilderness, not Sunol Wilderness Regional Preserve, just the town's name -- and its list is prefixed MIS:, OHL: and SUN: for Mission Peak, Ohlone and Sunol. THAT IS WHY MISSION PEAK HAS NO FACILITY OF ITS OWN: its sites are sold under this one. It also means searching the booking system for a park's name is not a way to find out whether the park has camping, which this project came within one inference of assuming two entries ago and was stopped from assuming by Mission Peak itself. SIX CAMPGROUNDS GAIN NAMED SITES THEY NEVER HAD. Eagle Springs is FOUR sites of 10; Boyd is two, 8 and 16; Doe is two, 14 and 10; Maggie's Half Acre is three, 6, 14 and 16; Stewart's is one at 24, the largest single backpack site here. A test asserted for weeks that these camps had no sub-sites 'because no source names any' -- which was true and was never the rule it looked like. The rule is that no placeholder row may repeat its campground's name, and that still holds. The test now says so. SUNOL'S SEVEN CAPACITIES ARE CONFIRMED EXACTLY -- Cathedral 5, Eagle's Aerie 10, Hawk's Nest 5, Oak View 5, Sky 3, Stars Rest 30, Sycamore 5 -- every figure matching what was already stored. AND SEVEN ROWS WERE QUIETLY CLAIMING TO BE BOOKABLE ONLINE. Sunol's sites carried online_bookable True while booking_channels has said since it was built that EBRPD's backpack sites are phone-only District-wide. ReserveAmerica LISTS all nineteen and sells none of them; listing is not selling, and the column means sellable. Corrected, and a test now asserts no backpack site claims otherwise. THE AERIE SPELLING RESOLVES IN FAVOUR OF THE STORED KEY, one day after it was recorded as contested. The facility says "EAGLE'S AERIE"; the Ohlone permit map's 'Eagles Eyrie' is the outlier at two to one. That map is also the document still demanding a permit abolished on 1 January 2026, so being wrong twice on one sheet is consistent rather than surprising. OPEN YEAR ROUND, stated for all nineteen, against four EBRPD parks whose group camps shut for five months. $15.00/night plus the $8.00 reservation service fee, confirming the stored rate. Maximum 3 nights, which agrees with the Ohlone-corridor exception already in ebrpd-backpack-stay-limit. THE FACILITY'S OWN GPS IS 37.51528, -121.83278 and its address 1895 Geary Road, Sunol, CA 94586 -- a ZIP the park page omits. It places the park near PLEASANTON where the park page says Sunol and the Fremont directions say Fremont; three cities for one entrance, which is the second EBRPD park in two days to publish its own location two ways after Morgan Territory's Livermore-or-Antioch. Neither changes a plan and neither gets a thread.

WHICH PARK ARE BOYD, STEWART'S, MAGGIE'S HALF ACRE AND DOE CAMP IN? This project files all four under DEL VALLE REGIONAL PARK. The booking facility prefixes all four 'OHL:' and puts them in a loop called 'Ohlone Backpack', where Sunol's seven are 'SUN:' and Mission Peak's four are 'MIS:'. On that pattern the prefix is a park and these camps are in Ohlone Regional Wilderness, which EBRPD's park finder lists as a camping park in its own right. IT IS NOT COSMETIC. The park field is what park_access joins on, so as filed these four inherit Del Valle's $10 weekend parking fee and its disputed 9pm-or-10pm gate. If they are in Ohlone they inherit nothing, because no Ohlone park_access row exists. DEL VALLE IS KEPT, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE FIELD IS DOING TWO JOBS. These camps sit 2.07, 6.58, 10.72 and 11.5 miles up the Ohlone Wilderness Trail measured FROM DEL VALLE, and a backpacker walking in from the Lichen Bark trailhead pays Del Valle's parking fee and meets Del Valle's gate whatever the boundary says. So the current value is right about what you pay and may be wrong about where you are. Boyd at 2.07 miles is plausibly inside Del Valle; Doe at 11.5 almost certainly is not. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is a boundary map, or an Ohlone Regional Wilderness park page -- neither read here. What would REDUCE it is a park field that distinguished the land a camp is on from the entrance it is reached through, which is the same gap Dumbarton Quarry and Star Mine already sit in and the third time it has mattered.

A MECHANISM FOR THE 15-VERSUS-18 PARK COUNT THAT NOBODY HAD OFFERED, and it is not a resolution. EBRPD's Reservations page says the department oversees camping 'at 15 parks'; the park finder tags 18. Three explanations were offered at the start and this is a fourth: RESERVATIONS MAY BE COUNTING BOOKING FACILITIES RATHER THAN PARKS. The Sunol facility, EB/110028, sells sites in Mission Peak, Ohlone and Sunol under one listing. Three parks, one facility. If the department counts what it administers rather than what the finder tags, two camping parks disappear from the count without any of them ceasing to have camping. THAT WOULD OVERSHOOT. Two from this facility plus Dry Creek Pioneer, which is evidenced, plus Dumbarton Quarry, which is contested, is four -- one more than the gap of three. So the four explanations cannot all be right, and the arithmetic that landed neatly on fifteen two days ago lands on fourteen with this one added. THAT IS THE USE OF THIS ENTRY: it is evidence that the clean sum was a coincidence rather than a reconciliation, which is what 'arithmetic that works is not evidence' was written down to guard against. The thread stays open and is now less settled than it looked, not more.

TEN OF THE NINETEEN PER-SITE PAGES ON THE SUNOL FACILITY: four Eagle Springs, two Boyd, two Doe, two Maggie's Half Acre. FOUR MILES TO EAGLE SPRINGS, STATED ONCE. Site #4 gives 'Hike In Distance to Site 21120' -- 21,120 feet, exactly 4.0 miles. The other three leave the field empty, so the figure sits on #4's row and is NOT read across to its neighbours, though four sites at one camp are unlikely to differ much. It is a different number from the park page's '3-plus-mile hike to Mission Peak', which measures the summit. The field is published in feet here and at Round Valley, where 18,000 became 3.41 miles. TWO STRUCTURED FIELDS ARE THE BOOKING SYSTEM'S SCHEMA LEAKING ONTO WALK-IN SITES, and reading them literally would be wrong. Six of these ten publish 'Driveway Surface: Gravel' for camps two to eleven miles up a trail with no driveway. Nine publish 'Maximum Number of Vehicles: 1', which means one car at the trailhead, not at the pitch. Both fields exist for drive-in campgrounds and get filled in anyway. Recorded as what they are rather than stored as facts about the site -- the same care the 'Looking For Category' facet needed yesterday, and the second time in two days that a ReserveAmerica structured field has turned out not to mean what its name says. THE NO-DOGS RULE IS STRUCTURALLY CORROBORATED, which matters because it is one of the rules flagged as resting on the booking platform rather than on any ebparks.org page. Ten sites read at site level, NOT ONE marked 'Pets Allowed: Domestic', where every EBRPD group camp read for this project carries that marker. The single pets marker on the whole corridor is Doe #1's, and it reads 'Horse'. Doe #2's category is 'Horse Site' ALONE -- no tent named at all, on a page headed BACKPACK SITE. That is not a second source for the rule and the regulation says so: it is the shape the data would have if the rule were true, and not the shape it would have if the rule were false. It also agrees with this project's own 'horse camp' note on Doe, which came from a different source entirely. EVERY ONE OF THE TEN TAKES A MINIMUM OF 1. That is the cleanest corroboration yet for keeping Round Valley's camp filed as backpack against a neighbouring map calling it a group camp: a site a solo camper can book is not a group site, whatever a category field says -- and Boyd #2 and Maggie's #2 are both tagged 'Group Site' while taking a minimum of one. SHADE IS NOW RECORDED where the facility gives it: full at Boyd #1, Doe #2 and Maggie's #2, partial at Boyd #2, Doe #1 and Maggie's #1. Privacy and Quiet Area are marked at both Doe sites and nowhere else on the corridor.
