STILL NOT STATED FOR ANY OF THE NINETEEN: restroom and water proximity, which is the question that decides which site to take at a camp reached on foot, and the reason open_questions asks it of hike-in campgrounds only. Nine per-site pages remain unread.

THE REMAINING NINE PER-SITE PAGES. ALL NINETEEN SITES ON THE SUNOL FACILITY HAVE NOW BEEN READ, and reading the whole set is what makes three patterns visible that no single page could show. PICNIC TABLES SPLIT PERFECTLY BY PARK. Every one of Sunol's seven sites is marked PICNIC TABLE. Not one of the twelve at Eagle Springs, Boyd, Doe, Maggie's Half Acre or Stewart's is. Seven for seven against none for twelve is a pattern rather than noise, though an absent marker is still not a stated absence. For a party carrying its kitchen four to eleven miles, a table is the difference between cooking on the ground and not. EAGLE SPRINGS IS THE ONLY CAMP WITH NO SHADE RATING ON ANY SITE. Fifteen of the other fifteen carry one, full at eleven and partial at four. This is the park whose own page leads with 'Every year, several dogs die of heat stroke and dehydration at Mission Peak.' A missing field is not a statement that there is no shade; it is the one camp here where a reader would most want the field filled, and the gap is recorded rather than guessed at. THE GROUP SITE FACET TRACKS CAPACITY, which closes off most of what was puzzling about it. It appears on every site of 14 or more -- Boyd #2 16, Doe #1 14, Maggie's #2 14, Maggie's #3 16, Stewart's 24, Stars Rest 30 -- and on no site of 10 or less. Nothing here has a capacity between 11 and 13, so the exact threshold is unknown, and EBRPD's own rule directing groups over 16 to a group campsite is near it but not equal. THIS NARROWS round-valley-camp-class WITHOUT CLOSING IT: Round Valley's camp is 1-25, so on this pattern it would carry the Group Site facet, which is almost certainly why a neighbouring park's map labelled it a group camp. The thread stays open because that entry said what would settle it -- the heading Round Valley's own campsites page files it under -- and that page still has not been read. A mechanism explained is not a source obtained. UNIFORM ACROSS ALL NINETEEN: hike-in, check-in 2pm, check-out 12pm, minimum 1. Eighteen of nineteen state one vehicle; only Doe #1 omits it. Twelve of nineteen publish a gravel driveway surface for a site with no driveway. STARS REST IS THE LARGEST SITE ON THE FACILITY AT 30 AND STILL BOOKABLE BY ONE PERSON; Sky is the smallest at 3. WHAT NINETEEN PAGES DID NOT GIVE: restroom or water proximity for a single site. That is the question that decides which site to take at a camp reached on foot, it is why open_questions asks it only of hike-in campgrounds, and after reading every page the booking system has, it remains unanswerable from this source. It would come from a park brochure or from someone who has been.

Point Pinole's park page and map. ADDS A PARK, THE BEST-EQUIPPED CAMP IN THIS PROJECT, A TRAIL CLOSURE THAT IS NOT STORM DAMAGE, AND A DOG RULE WITH A DIFFERENT DENOMINATOR. THE CAMP HAS A SHOWER, AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS ENTRY SAID NOTHING ELSE HERE DOES, WHICH WAS WRONG AND WAS CAUGHT BY A TEST WRITTEN TO ASSERT IT. Anthony Chabot's family campground has HOT showers and Puma Point Group Camp has access to them. What is actually new is a shower at a PRIMITIVE camp: Chabot's six other group camps sit behind their own gate with no access to showers or flush toilets, and Arroyo Flats, Round Valley and Morgan Territory all say 'no showers' outright. A superlative is a claim about the whole dataset and has to be checked against it, which is what the test did. Four 6ft picnic tables, a serving table, a double BBQ, a fire circle with three benches, a shade structure, two chemical toilets, a drinking fountain with spigot, a 5ft by 8ft STORAGE CONTAINER WITH A COMBO LOCK, and A RINSING SHOWER. Arroyo Flats and Round Valley both state 'no flush toilets or showers' outright and no other camp mentions one. The lockable container is also unique and matters more than it sounds at a camp whose access mode nobody has recorded: somewhere to put food that is not a car. THE NAME IS CONSTRUCTED AGAIN. The page says 'Point Pinole group campsite'; the map has a Reservable Group Camp symbol and no readable label. Morgan Territory's constructed name turned out to be exactly what ReserveAmerica calls it, WHICH IS NOT A REASON TO TRUST THIS ONE -- one convention holding once is not a method. Point Pinole's three ReserveAmerica pages. THE FIRST BOAT-IN SITE IN THIS PROJECT, and it arrives with two modes at once: 'Site Access: Boat-In, Hike-In'. THAT MADE access_mode MULTI-VALUED. The field was single-valued because every site read before had one answer, not because sites have one -- and it is EBRPD publishing a comma-separated pair that forced it, not a judgement made here. Stored as boat_in;hike_in, the same ';'-separated shape agency_id already uses for co-managed land. access_label now reads 'boat-in or hike-in', because a reader shown one mode has been told the site is harder or easier to reach than it is, and the discovery filter matches on MEMBERSHIP so that --access hike_in returns it. A THIRD WAY IN EXISTS AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT STORED AS drive_in.
